checks the original PE32 xcpt4 main, including filters, ordinary and runtime
finally invocations, local unwinds and jump-buffer resumptions. The shared
registration work cap is 4,194,304. A Release observation used 1,144,583 state
work units and 2,613,031 units for the complete decoded-callee closure. The
original filter-output test also passes when built independently from its
unchanged test body and helper. These work counts are deterministic accounting,
not a throughput benchmark. PE64 source projection and native-frame proofs
have separate acceptance gates.
Unknown-address frame accesses still charge every potentially aliased cell.
Their budget regression scales its load count with the configured limit and
must withdraw all complete output when exhausted.
`RegistrationFrameSnapshot` checks independent ordinary, entry and callback
snapshots through partial writes, merges, stack release and callback reentry.
Its deterministic mutation sequences compare shared branches with a bank of
independently reconstructed cell maps, including hashes and logical work counts.
Run these with the frame-memory tests, registration state/callee/EH suites,
native and realigned registration fixtures, jump tables and instruction/exception
boundaries when changing the snapshot storage. Sharing must not publish new
stack, import-binding or frame-preservation facts.
Memory extent tests continue to reject a borrow beyond 1 MiB and an oversized
C++ throw object. Their shared source-call storage limit is independent of
the registration propagation work cap.

The borrowed-capture, asynchronous-filter-write and nested-finally cases
require actual buffer contents, disjoint object extents and each invocation's
own return slot. Import rebinding, partial buffer writes, changed CALL bytes,
missing capture evidence and unproved continuations refuse. The returning
RaiseException case checks a call before a finally return; conditional and
guarded instructions and an absent memory contract still refuse.
CRT regressions check the exact `_controlfp_s` binding and output DWORD,
floating-state intrinsic shapes and import cleanup without granting memory
effects. `RegistrationCRTCall.NullControlFPHasNoOutputBorrow` covers null
output queries and all three valid PE32 precision encodings, while retaining
refusals for reserved/partial masks, frame-valued controls, ambiguous null
provenance and unauthenticated calls. The unconditional callee-stack target's
`RegistrationImportABI.ControlFPBindsCurrentRuntimeProvider` checks MSVCRT and
MSVCR100 identities, storage conflicts, delayed imports and changed source
calls. Scalar comparison tests cover signedness, input widths and unknown
values. Distinct direct registration prologues inside one guessed function
range must retain separate owners; a damaged prefix supplies no new entry.

`RegistrationTryLevel.ForeignCxxTablesDoNotSeedOrdinaryRoots` places an
unrelated returning function before a foreign C++ callback. Ordinary and
integer-frame CFGs exclude only the checked runtime source, with and without
a matching relocation index. Independent aliases, changed pointer bytes,
partial or mismatched FuncInfo graphs and missing metadata retain ordinary
roots. A foreign-image index must use the current input, and raw relocation
provenance remains available. Run `NeverDRegistrationEHTests` with the
registration stack/native and Mach-O pointer-relocation boundary suites after
changing this shared discovery path.
The same cases exercise a borrowed callee index and matching or foreign
scoped owners. `OrdinaryRootRolesRefreshAfterImageChanges` reuses a builder
while changing only the exception metadata, requiring each new operation to
recompute the runtime role.

`PipelineOutcome.SourceEHRefusalsAgreeAcrossSingleAndShardedEmission` checks optimized and unoptimized source projection across PE32, ELF and Mach-O on x86, x64 and AArch64. Single-function and sharded LLVM emission retain the same explicit incomplete native EH contract; binary rewriting still rejects it.

`RegistrationCallNoReturn` rejects changed instruction extents, targets, operation ranges, conditional calls and foreign architecture/format use. The realigned PE32 probe checks both an independently terminal decoded call and a retained fallthrough requiring a current receipt; invalid memory evidence cannot recreate an already absent ordinary edge.

`SafeSEHReference.*` checks immutable SafeSEH membership, malformed or ambiguous storage, relocations, foreign architectures/formats and declaration order across shards. `PipelineOutcome.NativeFinallyInputsRetainSourceLLVM` uses `NEVERD_NONLOCAL_FINALLY_INPUTS` to test 32 LLVM combinations of the native MSVC x86/x64 O0/O2 and GS fixtures with source optimization enabled and disabled. It verifies LLVM and resolved call signatures while requiring unsupported x86 native EH reconstruction to remain rejected. The focused Windows EH job downloads the native fixture artifact and runs this matrix; without the input directory the test is explicitly skipped.

`RegistrationPrologueSaves.*` and `PipelineOptNone.*` cover retained source memory, protected callback arguments/selectors and continued optimization of ordinary code. The native MSVC matrix checks the x86 `/Od` and `/O2` (`/GS-`, `/GS`) `nonlocal_finally_return` and `nonlocal_finally_goto` exports, including independent COFF validation. `check_windows_finally_rewrite.py --form return` and `--form goto` compare raw/optimized IR through both patch modes at two forced bases, with chain/stack guards and a negative control. The header-only EXE-to-DLL adapter requires a TLS-free input and retains original code; an outer SEH observer supplies exception search. This does not establish support for partial local-unwind bounds or reentry inside active enclosing scopes.

`RegistrationEH4Wrapper.*` covers both bases, mutable/immutable runtime data, MXCSR branches, every-path definitions, caller-frame isolation, overlapping instructions/storage and exact PE relocations. The two MSVC profiles each include an independent negative control.

`LocalUnwindInsideCheckedSEHHandlerCarriesTheParentFrame` checks local-unwind calls from a checked Windows x64 SEH handler and from shared ordinary/exceptional entry paths. Negative cases cover mismatched unwind allocation, unstable or partial SP values, independent roots, incomplete input, absent or forged exception edges, work exhaustion, loads from unknown stack memory, foreign target relocations and untrusted runtime providers. The LowIR call proof and module receipt both feed SSA verification; ordinary returned-continuation tests retain their separate root rules.

`OrdinaryInternalReturnsRetainTheParentsReturnPC` and `OrdinaryInternalWritesCanUseTheParentsPrivateAllocation` check parent-PC corruption and disjoint parent-local writes on PE, ELF and Mach-O x64 and ELF i386. An intact callee PC alone cannot authorize an ordinary call.

`LLVMFrameSlotProof.RepeatedClosedQueriesDoNotRepeatProofWork` bounds repeated positive and negative query work across x86, x64, ARM and AArch64. `SharedBudgetProofsReplayTheirNodes` checks that a replayed shared-budget proof leaves the same answer and remaining budget as a fresh walk, for an exactly sufficient budget, one node short and half the nodes, and that a walk that ran out replays only for budgets no larger than its own; `BoundQueriesReuseOnlyTheirBindings` keeps answers for different bindings apart. The context tests retain bound-value, entry-SP, width and zero-budget refusals, and discard answers across provisional/rebuilt feasible graphs and function changes.

`RegistrationState.LocalUnwindRetiresLevelsAfterCheckedFinallyEffects` also checks early stopping below a bound, sentinel exits, enclosing links that skip the requested index and joins with distinct stopping levels. Missing finally bodies must still be rejected when actually traversed; a skipped cleanup must not lend a frame-write effect.

`RegistrationState.LocalUnwindRetiresLevelsAfterCheckedFinallyEffects` also covers constant bounds outside the table, the high unsigned half and -2. No-op exits retain the original level and frame-memory facts; dynamic bounds and invalid current levels still reject.

`RegistrationState.MalformedSEHScopeGraphsPublishNoStateFacts` checks wrong sentinels, cycles, forward/out-of-range links, invalid initial levels and handler/filter roles despite a complete parser status. Initial-active-scope and empty-table controls preserve valid frame sentinels in both EH3 and EH4. Over-width handler and filter addresses also reject without publishing facts.

The source registration solver uses one administration-boundary check for object borrows, catch-object construction and local-finally writes. `RegistrationState.SEHObjectBorrowsExcludeSavedStackAndExceptionPointers` and `SEHObjectWritesCannotBorrowWholeOrPartialCookieCells` cover EH3/EH4 reads, writes and partial overlaps with SavedESP, exception pointers and cookie cells. `RegistrationCallback.RealignedCatchObjectsCannotReplaceRuntimeAnchors` protects the saved entry frame independently of later reloads. Adjacent ordinary objects remain valid.

`RegistrationSEH4Shared.*` in `NeverDRegistrationSEH4EntryTests` checks shared EH4
installation and restoration through the ordinary loader and CFG builder.
It covers short/wide allocation pushes, two image bases, current helper-byte
mutations, changed LowIR prefixes and extra entry roots. Small allocations
whose SavedESP write overlaps a nonvolatile save must refuse the returning
frame proof. Source-state completion is distinct from native EH publication.
`FrameCallsLeaveBudgetForOrdinaryCallees` and
`RegistrationTryLevel.CxxSharedCallsDoNotConsumeOrdinaryCalleeBudget` check
that exact shared entry/exit occurrences use their physical-frame analysis
without spending the ordinary-callee budget on those helpers. A separate
ordinary call still needs its scalar and returning-stack proofs within a
2,048-unit allowance. Changed helper bytes, call operations, instruction
boundaries, metadata and interior roots withdraw the classification; another
occurrence of the same target is not exempt. Exhausted budgets still refuse.
`RegistrationSEH4Physical.*` in `NeverDWindowsRegistrationNativeTests` checks
the separate physical projection at two bases, both allocation encodings and
three frame extents, then runs the LLVM verifier and independent COFF IR proof.
Removed or changed receipts, current helper edits, changed LowIR, extra entry
roots and overlapping saves must not regain native publication.
A returning ordinary call and an except entry exercise independently rechecked
callee stacks, fixed helper allocation and the COFF frame-lifetime proof; changing
the callee to return from the wrong stack slot invalidates the projection.
The filter reads the shared frame, forcing recovery across the native catchpad;
added byte and full-word writes to saved ESP must fail independent validation.
The real shared-frame fixture repeats those mutations in every outlined filter
and finally body, including normal and abnormal calls.
The real PE installer also rejects shifted relocation fields and changed table
operands at a narrow shared entry, using the same controls as the C++ entry.
`check_windows_registration_rewrite.py --shared-seh4` selects an authored PE32
shared-helper fixture for ordinary non-GS EH4 cases. Check filter, normal finally,
parameter writes and exception-code reads with both original and rebased images;
pass `--patch-binary` to include ordinary CLI section/inplace reconstruction from
EXE and IR. Original-helper execution alone does not qualify generated native
EH, and selected-function reconstruction does not qualify the GOF2 whole image.

`NeverDRegistrationCalleeStackTests` runs the decoded PE32 call/return ABI
controls, including a cycle between a registration parent and an ordinary
wrapper. An unbalanced recursive wrapper cannot borrow its own pending ESP
answer. `RegistrationCallABI.ReturningStackDoesNotFreezeRelocatedOperands`
checks arithmetic address operands and independent register restoration at
two image bases, rejects cancellation against equal unrelocated literals,
and covers conflicting, overlapping, partial and control-flow fixups. The
observed and discarded leaf-result queries reject the same cancellation,
with both classified and unclassified relocations.
`RelocatedStoresRetainExactImportAliasBounds` checks direct and register-carried
image writes at two bases, including stable address arithmetic. Disjoint writes
retain the imported stack adjustment; full and partial IAT overlaps, duplicate
or malformed fixups and conflicting address receipts reject it. Cached import
tests apply the same alias rule before and after loading a callable target.
`Native32AddressCarriersKeepExactProvenance` checks native and normalized
address widths, scalar and fragment counterexamples, and values beyond the
32-bit address domain. `CachedLoadReceiptsBindCurrentBytesAndLowIR` checks the
current three-operation absolute MOV packet, its load sequence, and mutations
of bytes, address width/provenance, destination, memory ordering and storage.
`RegistrationImportABI` covers the nine checked Kernel32 startup imports,
including `IsProcessorFeaturePresent` and `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`,
through direct IAT calls and decoded jump veneers. Wrong providers, delay
imports, conflicting or truncated storage, missing import-directory evidence,
mutable code and unbalanced argument cleanup refuse the stack proof. The same
storage controls apply to `RaiseException`. A four-argument
`HeapSetInformation` call cannot acquire exception dispatch merely because it
also pops sixteen bytes; neither it nor a cdecl CRT import gains caller-frame
observation permission. Returning-stack facts still grant no object borrow or
initialized memory. These are static authored-machine tests, not execution of
GOF2 or qualification of its full image.
`OrdinaryHelpersNeedIndependentBindingEffects` checks integer helpers, private
push/pop and scalar accesses, mapped reads, and a proved unreachable opaque
call before a subsequent eager import. Unknown or unmapped reads, image writes,
return-PC and caller-argument writes, unallocated stack writes, division, FP
waits, reached opaque calls and unknown branches cannot retain bindings. A
caller that already replaced its slot remains rejected even when the helper's
independent binding effect succeeds. The same matrix composes through a second
ordinary helper, and a loop backedge reopening an unknown read withdraws the
summary. Registration-state consumers retain live slots through this effect
while still discarding cached register targets at an ordinary call.
`RegistrationStartupInfo` checks the complete 68-byte output against outgoing
arguments, registration fields and cookies under EH3, EH4 and GS. Full and
partial frame-pointer spills retain their provenance after a possible runtime
write, including all three conditional standard-handle fields. The import tests
also require the exact current direct-call instruction and bounded proof work.
Earlier full or partial writes to its IAT slot invalidate the output borrow; an
unrelated image write does not.
`CheckedOutputPreservesOnlyLiveImportBindings` follows the checked output with
a second imported call and a stack write. EH3, EH4 and GS retain the second
call's stack coordinate only while its binding is live. Full or partial writes
to that other IAT slot, an invalid output extent and failed authentication
still refuse; an unrelated image write preserves the proof.
`check_windows_registration_rewrite.py --startup-info` adds an independently
sampled `GetStartupInfoW` output oracle to filter and normal-finally cases;
combine it with `--shared-seh4` or an EH4/GS case as needed. Both observations
start with the same poison so untouched fields remain observable. The native
validator rejects changed call/provider identity, output offsets, source bytes,
calling conventions and invented memory, unwind or parameter attributes.
`RegistrationHeapPolicy` exercises the exact no-borrow heap-policy tuple under
EH3, EH4 and GS. Changed words, an unknown input, partial initialization,
full/partial IAT writes, another expired import and failed authentication
cannot publish a native call. Unrelated storage writes remain admissible and
an exhausted budget refuses. The shared physical-invocation import test also
checks both startup-output and heap-policy providers against changed bytes,
slots, ABI shape, delay imports and work exhaustion.
`check_windows_registration_rewrite.py --heap-termination` adds the authored
request to filter and normal-finally cases, and can combine it with
`--startup-info`. Native mutation checks alter required constants, substitute
a volatile load, change null pointers, provider/source identity and ABI, or
add memory/exception/parameter claims. Fresh source replay also rejects a
changed physical PUSH even when the emitted LLVM constants remain unchanged.
`RegistrationSEHRuntimeFrame` checks saved frame-address recovery across the
independently bound no-borrow call. Missing effects, another unbound runtime,
overlapping callback writes and unknown callback calls still refuse; a disjoint
callback write preserves the saved address. Shared EH4 filter and finally cases
exercise this projection through the physical saved-stack and epilogue paths.
`RelocatedLeafAddressesKeepMemoryIdentity` retains exact image-read extents
through a relocated address and a stable offset, while rejecting missing
operand classification. `RegistrationFrameScalar` separately checks address
versus integer identity, all three frame coordinate spaces, partial-width
loss, frame spills, snapshot identity and EH4 cookie/address XOR terms.
`RegistrationConditionalFrame.BoundImmutableScansKeepTheirMemoryExtent`
in `NeverDSEHRuntimeMemoryTests` checks caller-bound immutable scans at two
image bases with zero, one and three iterations. Mutable or missing bytes,
conflicting fixups, duplicate mappings, a count beyond the mapped object,
writable code and a borrowed frame address all reject. An already exhausted
budget and a budget one work unit short cannot publish a partial proof.
Its successful scans also check the sum returned in EAX; every failed query
clears its result. `ReturnsKeepTheirInvocationAndAddressIdentity` covers exact
integers, image addresses, unknown initialized arguments, differing return
paths and no-return loops. Incoming EAX and the callee's return PC retain opaque
call provenance; a private-frame escape still refuses. The registration state
test `ConditionalResultsReachTheNextInitializedCall` follows these results
through physical EAX or an instruction-local temporary into the next call,
including partial/wide output carriers, other volatile registers, absent
results and a refusing callee prover. Target-wide cleanup and invocation-only
zero/four-byte cleanup reach the next call separately; popped argument bytes
must lose initialization before that call.
`RegistrationConditionalReturn` in `NeverDSEHRuntimeMemoryTests` checks
input-dependent near-return cleanup and an unselected indirect tail at two
image bases. Reversed/repeated inputs, unknown branches, far returns, changed
ESP/nonvolatile registers, overwritten return PCs, nonreturning loops and
exact/one-unit-short budgets retain their separate outcomes. The typed
invocation receipt retains cleanup and EAX together and clears both on refusal,
including budget exhaustion. The pinned
`BoundRaiseWrapperRetainsOnlyLocalProofs` case verifies that initialized cdecl
arguments can prove a wrapper's returning frame without creating a target-only
ABI or a call-free effect for its RaiseException invocation. Run registration
callee, state and EH suites alongside this owner; the shared frame interpreter
also serves C++ source and native-effect queries.
`RegistrationConditionalFrame.UnknownScalarArgumentsNeedInitializedBytes`
adds a search with an unknown scalar key. Complete byte initialization admits
both full-word and bytewise stores despite absent sparse scalar cells. Every
missing input byte, stale stack position, partial pointer taint and overflow
rejects; an exact old value cannot override a missing initialization byte.
Both image bases and exhausted/one-unit-short budgets are covered. Run the
registration state suite as well: its conditional C++ tests consume the same
caller-word reader and retain overlapping-taint and nested-call coverage.
`RegistrationConditionalSEH` in `NeverDSEHRuntimeMemoryTests` checks authored
scalar-only SEH helpers at two image bases, unknown initialized inputs,
missing bytes, overlapping pointer taint, current call/code identity and exact
work limits. Ordinary returns retain scalar/image values, join differing
paths and erase callee-owned identities. A protected ordinary/except pair
separately checks that a filter's result cannot enter the ordinary EAX join.
`NestedCleanupUsesTheCurrentScalarInput` selects actual zero/four-byte RET
cleanup from the current argument, despite an absent target-wide ABI. Unknown
arguments still refuse inconsistent cleanup at both image bases.
The root-call case passes an actual pushed scalar and uses the returned value
to guard a frame escape. A joined constant-return receipt permits a complete
native EAX observation; absent receipts, nonreturning calls, another callee kind,
partial/wrong-register outputs and skipped SSA still refuse. A shared call under
two live scope levels intersects differing returned constants while retaining
its unchanged argument recipe and unused-result admission. Result-use tests
separate observations from malformed definitions and widths, and check exact
and one-unit-short budgets. The authored rewrite driver's
`--observe-callee-result` mode uses a returning helper's actual EAX plus five as
the later longjmp value, across EH3/EH4/GS, optimized/unoptimized and rebased
outputs. Native mutation checks retain rejection of new unowned observations.
`RegistrationEH4Wrapper` additionally checks exact retained dependencies for
direct/indirect forwarding, hotpatch prefixes, veneer chains, both normalizer
branches, gaps between decoded paths and dynamic data reads. The separate
`RegistrationSEHPersonality.RetainedDependenciesRequireImmutableIdentity`
case rejects changed provider/slot identities, delayed or duplicate imports,
writable/ambiguous code, malformed fixups and incomplete storage at two bases.
Run `NeverDRegistrationEHTests` and `NeverDWindowsRegistrationNativeTests` for
these loader-owned records; they do not qualify a final PE or a native call.
`RetainedRuntimeRequiresEveryAddressRelocation` checks all wrapper, thunk and
cookie operands at two bases. Missing individual HIGHLOWs, dynamic normalizers
and exhausted work refuse; changing the valid runtime provider changes the
retained record. Existing EH3, shared-entry, cookie and wrapper cases verify
their exact operand inventories. `RetainedOperandsRequireCompleteRelocations`
checks partially relocated code, a large unrelated ordered inventory, malformed
wide overlaps, repeated queries and exact/short/empty work allowances. The
existing instruction-fixup mutation matrix also runs the stronger reader.
`ImmutablePE32Code.InteriorPointerStorageDoesNotGrantAnOrdinaryEntry` in
`NeverDReadOnlyBytesTests` checks callback storage at two bases while preserving
the ordinary-entry requirement. Its mutations cover fixup multiplicity, width,
overlap, competing roles, partial storage, target permissions and image kind.
The `RegistrationSEH4Shared.TypedScopeStorage*` cases in
`NeverDRegistrationSEH4EntryTests` check EH3/EH4 except/finally fields, optional
GS cookies, stale graphs/bytes, table ownership and exact/exhausted work. The
EH3 table view tests field interpretation only; it does not claim an EH3 frame.
`BudgetedStorageQueriesReplayCurrentInputs` checks fresh scalar and callback
queries, repeated charges, changed fixups and exact/short/empty allowances.
The budgeted callback reader also runs the existing storage mutation matrix.
`TypedScopeStorageBoundsOrderedInventoryQueries` adds a large unrelated ordered
inventory without exhausting the remaining work, then introduces an overlapping
field and requires refusal under the same allowance.

The separate `RegistrationOriginalImage` cases check scoped mapped-address
differences, unchanged generic transfer, immutable scalar widths, pointer-byte
refusal, conflicting fixups/mappings, image separation and exact/exhausted work.
`OriginalImageDifferenceStaysScoped` and
`OriginalImageReadRecordsExactInputsAndBytes` bind authored SEH invocations at
two bases and keep their source evidence out of native `ConstantReturn`.
These queries do not qualify final-PE replay or native layout-dependent calls.
`OriginalImageReadsRetainAddressProvenance` separates scalar and image addresses
for direct and nested header reads, including overwritten results, at two bases.
`ReadAddressIdentityRequiresEveryObservation` intersects mixed observations in
both orders and checks distinct widths and exact/short/empty allowances.
`PlainImageReadsRequireAnEffectOwner` checks exact immutable header reads,
ignored results, fixed results and exact/short budgets. Queries without an
image-effect owner refuse and clear their result. The nested SEH regression
changes the authored header count at two preferred bases: only scoped proofs
retain the read, no native constant is granted, and candidate replay rejects a
changed ordinary result while accepting unchanged results with different reads.
`CandidateReplayBindsTheOriginalCall` checks a retired candidate CALL, changed
immutable bytes with an unchanged result, changed results and coincidentally
equivalent modified code. A valid candidate call cannot repair an invalid
original call. Base changes, missing initialized inputs, writable/relocated
reads and tainted arguments refuse. `CandidateReplaySharesOneWorkBudget`
checks exact, one-unit-short and exhausted allowances for both source queries.
`ScopedProofRetainsSharedFrameProtocols` checks the shared caller and helper
extents and all decoded table/handler/cookie operands at two bases.
`CookieAddressObservationsKeepProtocolValues` records exact versus preferred-only
cookie addresses without reading the cookie's initial bytes as constants.
`RetainedReplayClosesProtocolDependencies` composes source, shared protocols,
typed tables and runtime code under one exact/short/empty budget. Its negative
controls remove individual address relocations or change an otherwise valid
provider after the weaker source replay has accepted the same ordinary result.
This includes a directly addressed cookie read whose LowIR address identity
survives removal of its HIGHLOW field; retained replay must still refuse it.
An unused absolute immediate checks the separate inventory comparison: deleting
both its fixup and its classification preserves the weaker source result but
must never reduce the retained candidate's relocation obligations.
`RetainedReplayChecksLiveCookieStorage` isolates the cookie from scope-table
storage and rejects unreadable, executable or overlapping mappings in either
image. Changing only the cookie's initial bytes remains valid and supplies no
constant cookie value.
`OrdinaryReadsCannotFoldLiveCookieBytes` and
`OrdinaryStorageExcludesLiveCookieOverlaps` reject root/nested ordinary reads
and partial overlaps with a read-only source cookie. Discarding the read does
not remove this dependency; adjacent nonoverlapping storage remains readable.
`BoundReadsKeepRuntimeCookieValuesOpaque` checks the same scalar owner through
144 ordinary helper variants: two bases, byte/word/dword loads, six overlapping
or adjacent offsets, present/absent cookie metadata and guarded/plain reads.
Plain reads retain an opaque result and exact footprint. A branch on initially
zero cookie bytes cannot hide an otherwise unproved load. The direct shared
reader and original-image scope must agree on cookie overlaps.
`RegistrationImageProof.ActualImageArgumentsRequireCanonicalValues` checks
actual LLVM arguments at two preferred addresses, including equal numeric bits,
volatile frame loads, global loads, aliases, private definitions, foreign
modules, address-space/TLS/import changes and noncanonical symbols.
`ImageArgumentIdentityUsesOneWorkBudget` checks exact, short and exhausted work
and an absent argument index. These are identity checks, not native admission.
`NativePointerArgumentsKeepOriginalStorage` checks direct and constant-byte-GEP
native pointers at two bases. Loaded or integer pointers, aliases, changed
storage, foreign modules, dynamic/typed indices, oversized carriers, signed
offset loss and preferred-VA overflow refuse. `PointerArgumentIdentityUsesTheSharedBudget`
checks the same bounded declaration owner and an absent argument index. These
tests grant no mapped-object extent or atomic-call permission.
`RegistrationOriginalImageCaller` in `NeverDSEHRuntimeMemoryTests` binds an
authored parent's actual PUSH to a header-reading SEH helper at two bases.
A changed header result exposes the private frame and makes the caller
incomplete. Fresh caller edits cover a different image word, equal scalar bits,
a missing PUSH, an unknown input and partial initialization. A loop revisits
one physical CALL with different input identities whose returned bits agree;
that invocation set must refuse. Exact and short budgets include planning and
propagation. Ordinary analyses remain incomplete before and after the scoped
query, and the existing native binder still refuses its observed result.
`EarlierOrdinaryVisitCannotDisappear` revisits one CALL at different SEH states:
an ordinary image-valued result precedes a scoped scalar result. Both private
frames remain valid, but the later recipe cannot describe every invocation.
`RelocatedArithmeticKeepsItsAddressIdentity` covers ADD/SUB at two image bases:
exact HIGHLOW address provenance admits the authored SEH helper while its
ordinary result remains unknown. Missing, stale or conflicting classifications,
partial/duplicate/wrong-width fixups, writable mappings and a relocated CALL
displacement refuse. A dereference of the arithmetic result still lacks a
storage proof; exact and one-unit-short budgets are checked independently.
`VolatileInputsDoNotRequireStackArguments` checks all three PE32 volatile GPRs
at two image bases with constant, image and unknown scalar inputs. It retains
callee definitions and exact branch selection, rejects partial pointer-bearing
inputs, nonvolatile substitutes, unproved dereferences and writable code, and
checks exact/short budgets. `PrivateRegisterBindingsKeepTheEntryABI` rejects
frame pointers, nonvolatile/frame/out-of-range register indices and a register
map outside the invocation domain. A failed query publishes no result.
`RegistrationCallABI.ReturningStackProofDoesNotNormalizeTheX87Stack`
keeps the stack proof for bodies whose x87 normalization alone is incomplete
or splits blocks by TOP, and for FXAM with a proved or unproved tag.
`RegistrationCallABI.ScalarReturnDescribesEAXBesideAnX87Result` pins the leaf
contract's EAX result for a leaf that also returns an x87 value.
`RegistrationCallABI.RecordedStackPopsChargeTheirFreshWork` checks that a
recorded stack-pop answer charges the work of the fresh proof: the answer and
an exhausted caller budget match a fresh proof, answers of another SEH
analysis level stay apart, and another image object never reads the record.
`NeverDX87CallGraphTests` provides the focused `X87CallStack.*` and
`X87CallGraphCache.*` checks for the shared-cache and invocation boundaries.

`MedStackDelta.*` (in `NeverDLiftTests`) resolves the stack-pointer offset
behind 64 joins in a row, each merging two arms; every path reaches the live-in
stack pointer exactly at the depth limit, and one more join exceeds it.
`MedABIPass.FrameLocalLeafSummary*` (in `NeverDFPParameterMaskTests`) checks
the indexed leaf summary against duplicate definitions and entries, PHIs,
value widths and identities, authenticated stack live-ins, the depth limit,
and reuse across functions or invocations. The index belongs to one immutable
function; a rejected function must still count toward duplicate-entry rejection.
The `Native pipeline compatibility` workflow runs when dependencies, threading or
allocator support, the C API, its worker tests or the workflow itself change, or
on dispatch. ABI,
lift and HighIR commits rely on `CI`'s native legs, so a problem only clang-cl,
the native-thread baseline or the real-engine worker cases would catch shows up
at this workflow's next run. It runs the complete focused ABI,
pipeline-outcome, thread and HighIR control-flow owners on Linux, macOS and
Windows x64 (MSVC and clang-cl), together with actual SDK allocation and native
worker requests. It requires registered cases to execute without failures or
skips and asserts that the normal build enables mimalloc by default. This
focused profile does not replace CPU-emulation or full semantic qualification.
`NeverDGraphCyclesTests` checks component grouping and a million-node chain.

`MedCxxContinuationFrame.ProtectedSourcesFollowCompactedBlockIdentities` uses
native jump blocks removed before SSA. Both asynchronous and synchronous
catches must retain the parent's local slot and the nonvolatile value written
before the throwing call. The original FH3/FH4 GS/no-GS O0/O2 ABI-probe CLIs
remain the corpus-level check for this projection.

`HighCParamUsage` checks shared expression DAGs, repeated callee queries and
recursive argument uses. Its default and compacted parameter lists must agree
with the operands that C prints. The two `WindowsEHModesCorpus.Decompiles*`
regressions run the original FH3 O2 GS/no-GS probes and the five PE32 xcpt4 and
xframe inputs through the full source CLI, including output generation. These
checks also run in the Windows EH CI lane.

`NeverDSEHRuntimeMemoryTests` checks nested authenticated UCRT calls, actual
home-area writes, immutable formats and receipt freshness. Wrong providers,
delay imports, incomplete or conflicting PE32/PE64 storage, `%n` variants,
unproved writable formats, saved-slot overwrites, IAT rebinding, forged import veneers,
parent-return-PC overlaps with either CALL's push or the home area, saved cells
below SP and encoded frame escape
must refuse. These focused contracts do not establish xcpt4 support; retain the
real `DecompileMatrixFailsClosedWithAuditableExceptionMetadata` acceptance test.
`AnImagesWritableRangesServeEachCatalogOfIt` checks that an image's shared
writable ranges give the catalog its own scan gives, that another image's
ranges are not taken, and that a stopped or over-allowance scan gives none.

`SEHRuntimeMemory.WindowsFormatsDoNotBorrowForeignDialectContracts` checks the
decoded CALL through the complete frame proof. Ordinary integer/float formats
preserve the saved cell; positional/grouping/q dialects, unproved dynamic
widths, overflowing decimal fields, pointer conversions and multibyte formats
must not. Both segment and section extents cover each fixture's actual bytes,
so rejection tests syntax rather than an accidentally truncated mapping.

`SourceFrameFormatBytesOwnTheRuntimeContract`,
`MissingOrChangedFrameBytesWithdrawFormatAuthority` and
`FrameFormatsRequireLiveStorageAndEveryReachingByte` in the same target decode
source stores and calls. Byte/DWORD initialization, matching branch stores and
an inspected helper filling a missing byte preserve saved-frame evidence.
Changed or unknown bytes, missing NUL, conflicting branches, released storage,
runtime home/scratch areas and active return PCs refuse. The same Windows
grammar applies to image and frame formats. These tests do not establish
initial mutable-image bytes, handler-memory restoration or native execution.

`SEHImageFormat.*` in the same target decodes stores into writable PE image
storage. Complete stores, agreeing branch arms and an inspected callee filling
one byte preserve the saved frame across authenticated UCRT calls. File-only
bytes, missing bytes/NUL, conflicting branches, unknown byte writes, `%n`,
callee changes and saved-frame overwrites refuse. Truncated and ambiguous image
storage supplies no destination authority. The original xcpt4 matrix remains
the acceptance check for initial writable literals and exception activations.

`MedSEHEstablisherFrame.SourceIndependentEntriesKeepUnknownStackValues`
checks ordinary and shared exception entries without borrowing the prologue's
stack cells. Strict conversion still refuses, source conversion retains
unknown memory operands, and direct LLVM emission rejects the result.
`SourceSwitchRequiresEveryResolvedTarget` checks the resolver-to-frame CFG
boundary, including absent, duplicated, changed and unsafe target sets.
`SourceRequiresExplicitIndependentEntry` rejects disconnected protected paths
without a published source entry and accepts the same graph once that entry
can receive explicit unknown values.
`TheX87ContextHandleIsNotAFrameValue` proves the frame of a handler that starts
with `fninit`, whose x87 context handle the CFG builder begins at each root.
`TheHandlerBeginsTheX87ContextBeforeUsingIt` and
`OnlyTheX87ContextHandleIsAdmitted` refuse a handler that reads the handle
before beginning it and a handle copied into an ordinary register.
`MedSEHHandlerEntry.AArch64HandlerResumesWithTheProtectedRegisters` checks
that an AArch64 `__except` body reads x19 as the protected range left it,
through the frame its prologue set. A range that writes x19 leaves x19
unknown.
`MedSEHHandlerEntry.AHandlerResumingAtANopEndsTheArmThere` ends an `__except`
arm that resumes at a `nop` without a jump, and
`X86_64_PipelineE2E.DecompileC_MinGWStartupSEHWithX87Callee` decompiles
MinGW-w64-shaped startup code (`test_mingw_startup_seh.s`) whose guarded callee
resets the x87 state.
`COFFExceptionIR.HighCEmptyExceptArmResumingAfterItsTryPrintsNoJump` prints
MSVC's nested -O0 levels with empty arms, and
`HighCLeftOutTryTailKeepsTheLabelAJumpLandsOn` keeps the label that switch
cases leave a try body for. `HighCSEHFilterIsNamedAsTheFunctionListNamesIt`
names a filter by its function symbol over a `.text` section symbol, and by
an export. `HighCSEHHandlerArmReadsItsOwnSecondArgument` covers the xcpt4
termination handler that guards its own `__try`: its second argument, the
parent's establisher frame, keeps its name in the `__except` arm. A setjmp
provider executes the HighC output at O0/O2, and both paths must reach the
parent's slot; an attached C++ catch body still names the printed function's
`var_m8`. `NeverDSEHTerminationHandlerTests`
(`unittests/lift/eh/SEHTerminationHandlerTests.cpp`, built from decoded x64
bytes) covers the certified `__finally` EstablisherFrame and the projected
clause: `SEHTerminationFrame.*` proves the frame bytes from the prologue and
unwind codes, agrees with the in-function `__except` frame, and refuses a stack
adjustment into the scope, a frame register, unwind data the prologue
contradicts, a handler of no scope, and an exhausted budget;
`SEHFinallyBody.GuardsTheAbnormalWorkAndKeepsTheNormalCopy` shows bar1's `99`
under `if (AbnormalTermination())` with the `100` copy kept,
`FlagIndependentHandlerFillsTheClauseAndDropsTheCopy` fills a flag-independent
clause and removes the matching copy, `AFrameRegisterParentFillsTheClause`
locates the handler's frame below the register's offset,
`NestedExceptInTheProtectedBodyFillsTheClause` fills a finally around an
`__except` that rejoins the protected body, and
`AFrameRegisterThePrologueDoesNotSetKeepsTheComment` keeps the address comment
where nothing locates the frame, and
`AnUncertifiedLocalUnwindStaysBesideTheFilledClause` keeps a call the protocol
cannot certify in its runtime form beside the filled clause it runs.
`AHandlerPassingAStackArgumentFillsTheClause` fills a handler whose call takes a
stack argument, and `ANameOfTheMovedStackPointerAddressesTheHandlersFrame` and
`ARenamedVariableIsNotTheNameItsNumberShares` hold the two rules ntoskrnl's
handlers need: a renamed stack pointer addresses the handler's slots, and an
unread name goes although a nested clause reads another of its number.
`SEHTerminationFrame.AFrameRegisterLocatesTheEstablisherBelowItsOffset` reads
the frame below a frame register's coded offset.
`SEHLocalUnwind.*` imports `_local_unwind` and
certifies its saved-frame slot: a return out of the `__try` becomes a jump
whose filled clause runs the handler's abnormal work, with the normal-path
copy kept for the fall-through; a flag-independent handler fills the whole
clause and loses the copy; a jump to where the try ends stays a jump rather
than `__leave` or a fall-through; and a handler that keeps its comment runs
as one explicit `handler(1, frame)` call before the jump. Each counts the
handler's work so every exit runs it once.
`AGSCookieMasksTheFrameItsDataPlaces` saves the frame in MSVC's slot and
masks it into the cookie slot its GS data places, which still certifies;
`AMaskedFrameNoGSDataPlacesKeepsTheCall` and
`AnUnmaskedFrameInTheCookieSlotKeepsTheCall` keep the runtime call when no GS
data places the masked frame or the frame reaches the cookie slot unmasked.
`AnAuthenticatedSetjmpTakesTheFrame` hands the frame to the runtime's
`__intrinsic_setjmpex`, which still certifies, and
`AFrameAFunctionOfTheImageReadsKeepsTheCall` keeps the runtime call when the
same frame reaches a function of the image that reads it, and
`AFrameItsCalleeNeverObservesPassesNothing` certifies the frame left in R8
for a function whose unread proof covers R8.
`AFinallyThatUnwindsToTheTargetLandsThereAsAJump` lets the Guarded exit own its
epilogue, and turns a `__finally` that local-unwinds there too into the `goto`
it makes. `ABranchyHandlerFillsTheClause` folds the handler's own branch on the
flag while unwinding.
`SEHTerminationFrame.AFilterCallbackTakesTheSameEstablisher` certifies a filter
callback's frame and the homes its parent saves for it, and `SEHFilterValue.*`
prints each filter callback as its `__except` expression: the Counter read
through the homed argument, `GetExceptionCode() == 0xC0000005`, a constant as
`EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER`, MSVC /O0's temporaries in the parent's frame gone
when nothing else touches them, and the writes to a slot the parent reads kept.
`ARM64SEHLocalUnwindTests.cpp` builds MSVC ARM64 /O0 parents that reach the
import through a veneer: `ARM64SEHLocalUnwind.*` certifies the exit through
an unrecorded veneer from the saved entry stack pointer, with the handler
matched at the `bl` and given the frame pointer; turns a return out of the
`__try` into a jump whose clause runs the handler once, through x1 or
through the parent's x19, with the `100` copy kept; lets a target return x0
as the routine leaves it; and keeps the call when a handler writes the
saved-frame slot through x19.
`ARMSEHLocalUnwindTests.cpp` builds Thumb parents that call `__jump_unwind`
through an import stub: `ARMSEHLocalUnwind.*` turns a return out of the `__try`
into a jump whose clause runs the handler once, with the target in a
`movw`/`movt` pair and in a literal pool, and with a GS prologue whose helper
allocates four bytes the body's arithmetic does not show; a handler's own call
becomes a jump out of its clause. `AnExceptArmRejoiningLeavesTheRegistersValue`
publishes r4 across the PHI an `__except` arm leaves before a later `__try`, and
`ATryAfterAnExceptArmFillsItsClause` prints that clause.
Its `ARMSEHFinallyBodyTests.cpp`
builds AArch64 and
Thumb parents whose handler reads them through callee-saved registers:
`ARMSEHFinallyRegisters.*` publishes a frame address set before the range, an
incoming argument and a constant, the establisher frame only when the unwind
codes allocate exactly the range's frame and x29 holds it too, finds a Thumb leaf handler that only
the scope table names, and publishes nothing for a register written in the
range, one the parent never set, or a copy of an argument register that a
PHI joins; `ARMSEHFinallyBody.*` stores `99` to the
parent's own local, through its parameter or through the establisher frame
under `if (AbnormalTermination())`, fills a finally nested in an `__except`
and both of two nested finallys, fills through x1 whatever allocation the unwind
codes give, prints a frame the parent cannot name that a handler forwards to a
call as an unknown argument, keeps the comment for the unpublished registers, and
`ARangeRunningPastTheEpilogueStillStructures` structures a `__try` whose range
runs past the epilogue a branch around it skips to. `ARMSEHFilterValue.*`
publishes the frame pointer for a filter callback and prints the callback that
reads the homed Counter through x1 as its `__except` expression.
`WindowsEHModesCorpus.LocalUnwindReturnRunsTheFinallyOnceInTheClause` checks
xcpt4's `eret` the same way on the original x64 FH4 binary: one increment in
the `__except` arm, one in the filled clause and one in the normal-path copy,
with no `_local_unwind`, target address or handler call left, and
`LocalUnwindExitAgreesAloneAndInTheWholeUnit` prints the same function from a
`--func` view as from the whole unit,
`Xcpt4FilterCallbacksAreTheirExceptExpressions` prints every filter callback of
xcpt4's x64 FH4 /O0 binary as its `__except` expression and the /O2 filter
inside test58's termination handler as the Counter its frame homed, and
`AArch64LocalUnwindExitAgreesAloneAndInTheWholeUnit` does so for the ARM64
/O0 build's loop of two nested finallys, with no `_local_unwind` left.
`EveryFinallyClauseOfXcpt4HoldsItsHandlerAsCode` decompiles the x64, ARM and
ARM64 builds, /O0 and /O2, and clang-cl's ARM64 /O2: no clause is only the address
comment, no handler stays listed in an unstructured region's comment, and no
function with a scope table keeps a runtime local unwind.
`SplitTriesAndArmsKeepTheirSourceShape` reads Test85's three handlers around a
loop whose return path splits their tries, and Test86's `__except` arm that holds
a `__try` of its own and returns past every scope around it.
`LocalUnwindExitsKeepTheirLoopRegionsStructured` decompiles the O2 FH4 /GS
build, whose loop exits leave split finally scopes and jump to a copied
return tail, and requires every region of both functions structured.
Run the Windows SEH corpus and the xcpt4 Wine check after a change here; the
latter runs the original xcpt4 under Wine and checks the source projection
of its `main`, so it does not run the filled `__finally` bodies.
`StaticSymbolTableTest.MinGWImageNamesNoSectionOrFileRecord` reads
`unittests/loader/fixtures/mingw_sections.exe` (its Makefile rebuilds it with
MinGW-w64 GCC): GNU ld's section symbols stay as bounds that name nothing, its
`.file` record is dropped, and a static function's own record names it.
`StaticSymbolTableTest.MinGWDataAmongCodeIsData` reads `mingw_text_data.exe`
and its i386 build `mingw_text_data32.exe`, which keep a -1-headed pointer
table in `.text` as GNU ld keeps `__CTOR_LIST__`: the table is data, the
pointer to it in `.data` points to data, and its entry is a slot that holds
code.

`unittests/lift/eh/X86SEHDisplayTests.cpp`, in the same binary, gives the pipeline
an x86 `_except_handler3` frame byte for byte: `X86SEHDisplay.*` pins the `__finally`
holding its body with the `call` gone and the address comment kept, the abnormal
flag cleared inside the `__try`, the filter forms (a constant, `GetExceptionCode()`,
a call passing `GetExceptionInformation()`, a write before the value), nested
levels nesting their tries, a body that leaves the function ending the path of its
`call`, an ordinary local that is no try level, a scope laid out in pieces being one
try that starts where jumps enter it, an arm that does nothing, a jump out of a
`__finally` staying a jump, code running on into a `__finally`, a loop on a
register staying in its try, an entry inside a loop being a jump in the try, an arm
starting at its handler, a filter keeping its calls in order, clang-cl's record in frame
slots with its outlined filter and `__finally`, a clause that does nothing keeping its
address, and a `push` that only makes room being no argument. `WindowsEHModesCorpus.EveryFinallyClauseOfXcpt4HoldsItsHandlerAsCode`
holds the same for the whole of x86 `xcpt4`, with no loop that does nothing, no empty
`__try` and every call a filter or the startup code's arm makes.
`ClangClX86SehProbePrintsItsTries`, `X86StartupFramesPrintTheirTries` and
`X86WinapiCallsPopWhatTheyTake` pin clang-cl's frames, the CRT's own frames and the
stack pointer a Windows API call leaves. Run these checks when changing
the call-removal range index; handler boundaries, remaining calls and clause
results must stay unchanged.

`NeverDRelocatedFunctionEntryTests` checks LLVM's shared entry evidence across
x86, x64, Thumb and AArch64 with PE, ELF and Mach-O images. It covers bounded
relocation proofs, complete CFG tables, malformed metadata and cache reuse.
Its `COFFIndexedTables` cases cover short and long in-code pointer tables,
constructor sentinels, exact relocation gaps, conflicting instruction bytes,
unreachable or non-reading operands, existing pointer-run classifications,
out-of-line callbacks and jump-table ownership. They discard nested evidence
when code overlaps or metadata vetoes a table. A synthetic linked PE exercises
the loader through function discovery. Backward-edge cases reach code between
previously visited ranges, retain table storage in skipped gaps, and reject an
overlapping instruction whether its start or its operand was visited first
on both x86 and x64. LLVM cases require runtime indices in
escaped table addresses, including code segments beyond the embedding limit,
and reject unrelated code identities and unresolved pointers across formats.
The focused target also runs `PointerRelocationBatch` to check the existing
relocation classification contract. The pointer-boundary target's
`WidenedIndexDoesNotAuthorizeMixedCallableAndScalarSlots` keeps a zero-extended
index from bypassing callable-slot validation in mixed records.
`COFFJumpTableEvidence` runs authored PE images through the actual loader:
dead, segmented, narrow and wrong-stride jumps cannot hide callbacks; CALL/JMP
sharing and adjacent named objects retain their independent entries. Nested
dispatchers reached through CALL/JMP tables keep their cases in the correct
function. Its i386 mask case rejects scalar call targets in linked and
relocatable COFF, with an all-callable control. `COFFMinGWStyleTables` uses fixed
assembly so optimization cannot remove its executable CALL table or `.rdata`
JMP table. It checks exact
slots, readers, all five functions and LLVM verification. On Linux x86 hosts,
the original instructions and lifted LLVM execute as freestanding i386 ELF,
with independent dispatch/switch results at O0/O2 and high-bit/wrapping inputs.
Other hosts explicitly skip that execution check; the PE pipeline check still
runs when cross-target Clang and lld-link are available.
`CFGMetadataAuthenticatesEntriesWithoutRelocations` checks that metadata alone
identifies a code address, while its absence still refuses that address.
`RelocationsDoNotAuthenticateContinuationStarts` and
`CFGMetadataDoesNotAuthenticateContinuationStarts` reject independent function
identity for continuation code through both the verifier and LLVM emission.
The `FunctionEntryAdmission` cases exercise runtime, verified, symbol, unwind,
known-range and import evidence against the same data, continuation and
alignment rejections. They also check Thumb mode aliases, primary entries
preceding their unwind frames, index rebuilds and next-entry bounds. A named continuation jump
must retain its parent CFG and return; LLVM must keep interior frame addresses
relative to the primary function. CFG targets reject virtual tails, incomplete
instruction units and overlapping owners while admitting writable and
execute-only code. On-demand x86 import-thunk decoding cannot join code bytes
with adjacent data. Run `NeverDFunctionAdmissionTests`,
`NeverDNativePointerRelocationBoundaryTests`,
`NeverDMachOPointerRelocationBoundaryTests` and `NeverDSourcePatchLayoutTests`
when changing this shared entry boundary.
The bounded mixed-pointer walk and scalar index-cycle Mach-O fixtures also
link with LLD on non-Apple hosts, without a target SDK. Their loader, MedIR and
LLVM checks run there; the scalar case compiles the generated IR to AArch64
Mach-O at O0/O2. Typed LLVM checks keep both register-offset load indices as
numeric recurrences with zero/one seeds, separate from their table bases.
Apple Silicon additionally executes the original fixtures
and the rebuilt scalar program. Cross-target compilation does not establish
native execution on an Apple host.
`FunctionAdmission.NativeOutputRequiresEverySelectedEntry` checks mixed valid,
truncated and unmapped selections for patch and lift output across COFF, ELF
and Mach-O, with and without the shared analysis cache.
`ASelectedRejectedParentCannotExportOnlyItsCleanup` keeps source analysis
available while requiring native output to report the rejected parent and
its decode failure instead of exporting only an automatically selected callback.
`SelectedLiftReportsUnsupportedInstructionSemantics` checks that complete
decoding does not hide an unsupported x87 payload/tag read, and that the
selected-entry diagnostic identifies the unsupported instruction.

`PointerRelocationBatch.PointerRunsAmongCodeAreData` records an i386 jump
table's three relocated slots in `.text` as data slots and the displacement
naming it as a data operand, and keeps the two fields of one
`mov dword ptr [disp32], imm32` as operands.
`TwoAdjacentEightBytePointersAreDataAmongX64Code` takes two eight-byte fields
as data, and `PointerRunsAmongOtherCodeStayOperands` leaves an ARM literal pool
and an object file's relocations alone.
`X86_32_FunctionDiscovery.SwitchTableAmongCodeBelongsToItsFunction` builds a
linked i386 image whose table follows its function two bytes past a four-byte
boundary, with an aligned relocated `.rdata` pointer an instruction names past
it: the cases stay the switch's labels rather than entries, and the CFG
builder recovers all three. It fails without the run bound or the label rule.
`X86_32_FunctionDiscovery.CallbackStoredByARelocatedImmediateIsAFunction`
stores a callback with `mov [ecx+0x10], offset cb` and recovers the callback
as a function of its own.
`NeverDX86FunctionDiscoveryTests` runs the complete PE32 discovery suite.
Its operand-entry cases reject aligned prologue and padding guesses inside
reachable instructions while preserving independent symbols, exports, calls
and relocated pointers. Unreached bytes, overlapping instruction paths,
unresolved computed jumps, cross-section decoding and data markers cannot
disprove an entry.
`X86_32_FunctionDiscovery.SwitchTableAmongCodeLiftsPastTheMirrorLimit` lifts
such a switch from a `.text` larger than the LLVM emitter mirrors as one
global; it refuses the table's address without the table-base witness or the
elided address operations. A variant with no arbitration budget, which leaves
no slot suppressible as a large module's arbitration does, refuses it without
the exception for a table among the code. `APointerSpilledAcrossALoopsCallsKeepsItsTable`
walks an integer array in `.rdata` beside a code pointer with a pointer kept
in a frame slot across a call (`add dword ptr [ebp-4], 4`), and fails as an
ambiguous pointer table without the frame-slot recurrence.
`ANestedLoopsSpilledIndexStaysAnOffset` keeps an outer loop's index in a frame
slot and an inner loop's record pointer `&table[i]` in another, around a call
with a pushed argument; it is refused the same way without the affine frame
keys, as the inner loop's merge on the outer back edge leaves its pushes
unkeyed.
`ARuntimeIndexedReadOnlyTableResolves` reads an `.rdata` int table at a live-in
object pointer's field scaled by four, as GOF2's `sub_4028D4` does. Without the
run-mirror redirect it is refused as an ambiguous read-only table base; with it
the read is a GEP into a read-only global and the table VA survives nowhere.
`InCodePointerTableMirrorsPastTheLimit` reads a function-pointer table MSVC
lays among its code as data, in a `.text` over the 1 MiB single-global limit;
the read resolves through the table run's own mirror rather than refusing that
the code segment cannot mirror.
`ANarrowLoadBaseAmongCodeIsData` decodes a two-level switch's `movzx r,
byte [sel + table]` and its pointer-wide jump-table load; the byte table's
base in `.text` names data, the jump table's names code. Without the
narrow-load rule the byte-table base is a code address with no lifted
identity.
`SwitchCasesStayLabelsPastAnEntryBeforeTheTable` puts an aligned prologue
match in dead code between a switch's seven-byte `mov eax, N; jmp tail` cases
and its table among the code; the cases stay labels only because the
instruction reading the table, not the table's slots, names them.
`DataSegmentDispatchKeepsIndependentCallbacks` relocates that dispatch table
into ordinary read-only data: cases stay labels while an ordinary pointer read
and a separate callback slot retain independent function-entry evidence.
The operand-entry, exhausted-verification-budget and FDE-extent discovery
tests also cover relocation-backed entries outside a proven dispatch.
The LLVM interior-pointer, runtime-callable fallback and unmaterializable
table-target boundaries reject unresolved or masked code owners rather than
emitting their original numeric addresses as presumed padding.
`PrologueMatchesInsideAFunctionAreItsCode` falls into an aligned `push esi;
push edi` and branches back to an aligned loop head, both prologue matches the
entry owns, while a padded function and a tail jump's target stay entries;
`AFramePrologueAfterACallStaysAnEntry` keeps a frame prologue right after a
call that may not return. `APushOfEbpWithoutTheFrameMoveIsNoUnalignedEntry`
finds no entry at the 55 8B C6 inside `push 55h; mov eax, esi`, which the
unaligned scan took for a frame setup. `AnInt3ByteInsideAnInstructionIsNoPadding`
runs the loader's padding scan over a loop whose `jne` displacement is 0xcc:
the entry falls into the start guessed after it, which it owns, while the start
guessed after real padding past the entry's return stays an entry.
`CallbacksPushedPastTheReturnAreFunctions` pushes a constructor and a
destructor that sit right after the pushing function's return, with no call,
prologue or padding to mark them, and recovers both as functions; a catch
block's `mov eax, offset continuation; ret` keeps its continuation a label.
`AVtableSlotConfirmsAPaddingGuess` runs the loader over a destructor after
int3 padding that a relocated `.rdata` vtable slot names: it is no boundary
guess, while a padded start nothing names stays one.
`LLVMImportVeneerBoundary.APushedVeneerAddressNamesItsImport` stores an
exact import veneer's code-address constant, as `push offset` does; the
module names the import rather than refusing that the veneer has no code
identity.
`ARuntimeOrStaticPointerReadsThroughTheMirror` reads `p = arg ? arg : &empty`
with the default in a `.data` that holds a relocated code pointer, the shape
GOF2's merges take; `AMergeOfMirroredAndReadOnlyStaticsResolvesEach` adds a
relocated `.rdata` string arm, and both lift without an image address. Without
the merge rule they refuse as an ambiguous pointer-table address.
`AMergeWithAnUnprovedImageAddressKeepsItsProof` drops the string's relocation,
so its number lands in the image unproved: the read keeps the refusal, and
without that guard it would keep `0x402000` raw.
`I386CallContract.ABlockPhiIsNoArgumentPastAnEarlierCallInItsBlock` joins a
callback's address and an import call's leftover in EDX, calls the import
again in the join block, then a routine reading ECX and EDX: the argument is
the second call's leftover, while without the rule it is the join.
`SessionCAPITest.LLVMCReadsAPointerTableAmongCodeAsData` emits LLVM-C for the
function that reads the table through `.data`, which was refused before.
`NativePointerRelocationBoundary.MinGWPointerTableAmongCodeMirrorsItsFunction`
finds the entry of both fixtures' tables as the function's address in the
`.text` pointer-table mirror, and
`MinGWPointerTableAmongCodeTooLargeToMirrorIsRefused` pads `.text` past the
embedding limit with MinGW-w64 GCC, when installed, and expects the refusal.
`LLVMCValues.AGlobalAnEarlierInitializerNamesIsDeclaredFirst` compiles and runs
a whole module whose `.data`-like global points into a constructor list
defined after it.
`HighControlFlowSemantics.SlotCallGoesThroughThePointerItHolds` calls through
MinGW's `__imp_X` variables, which hold the image's own code, relocated or in
a fixed image, rather than naming an import by their spelling.
`StaticSymbolTableTest.MinGWImportVariableNoCodeChangesIsConstant` reads
`mingw_imp_slots.exe`, which calls through two such variables: the one nothing
changes is constant, the one its lazy binding rewrites is not.
`SessionCAPITest.MinGWImportVariableCallsReachTheirFunction` decompiles its
caller: HighC and LLVM C call the constant one's function directly and the
lazy one through its variable.
`HighControlFlowSemantics.AShiftByZeroIsItsOperand` reads AArch64's bit-0
`tbz` test as `x & 1`.
`HighControlFlowSemantics.ATruthValueSelectingOneOrZeroIsItself` reads -O0
AArch64's `cset w8, eq; and w8, w8, #1` as the comparison itself, or its
negation, and keeps a selection by a value that may hold another number.
`NativePointerRelocationBoundary.MinGWProgramWholeModuleLLVMCCompiles` links
a program against the MinGW-w64 runtime, when its compiler is installed, and
compiles the program's whole-module LLVM C for x86-64 MinGW, including actual
object generation at O0 and O2. Syntax-only checking cannot detect a data
alias colliding with Clang's implicit SEH personality.
`COFFExceptionIR.LLVMCAddressedImportKeepsItsRuntimeFunctionDeclaration`
isolates an address initializer preceding SEH and compiles both optimization
levels. Object relocations with the same name and other object formats retain
their data declarations. `HighCAddressedRuntimeFunctionPrecedesSEH` checks the
same ordering through HighC. `LLVMCAddressedImportUsesPrototypeHeadersAndWeakLinkage`
checks prototype-owned headers, weak linkage and an unknown import control.
These are compilation checks; native Windows exception execution remains a
separate gate. The LLVMCValues
cases it rests on compile and run on the host:
`ACallerWithUnwindInformationSeesItsCalleeDeclared` declares a callee whose
caller carries an unwind record;
`ALibraryRoutineCalledThroughItsImportTakesItsDeclaration` calls `fputc`,
`getenv` and `free` through import symbols with their headers' types and
`EnterCriticalSection` with the runtime tables' prototype;
`ARuntimeRoutineReturningAFunctionPointerIsDeclared` declares `_onexit`, and
`ARuntimeRoutineCalledDirectlyTakesItsPrototype` declares it for a direct
call, which passes only its parameter;
`ACastBetweenAnIntegerAndAPointerConverts` passes a volatile read's integer
to a pointer parameter and adds to a pointer it read;
`AWeakImportIsDeclaredWeak` links without `__gmon_start__`;
`ADefinitionOfALibraryRoutinesNameTakesItsAddress` renames the image's own
`atexit`, `AMinGWRoutineTheProgramLinksTakesItsAddress` a Windows program's
`__mingw_printf` and no other format's, and
`AWholeModulesMainTakesItsAddress` a whole module's `main`; and
`ACalleeThatReturnsNothingLeavesItsResultUndefined` calls a definition
settled as returning nothing alone, or reads zero for its result.
`LLVMCIntrinsicSemantics.RepMovsForwardBackwardDynamicAndOverlap` runs
`rep movs` copies of each width and direction, overlapping ones too, and
`RepMovsRejectsUnprovedContracts` refuses other shapes.
`LibCResult.ReadsWhetherTheDeclaredResultIsAPointer` reads pointer results
from headers, typedefs included, and from the runtime tables.
`MinGWHeaderFunctions.NamesWhatTheHeadersDeclare` reads the routines the
mingw-w64 headers declare, its own, the runtime's and the C library's.

`NeverDItaniumHandlerTests` spells Itanium landing pads as C++ handlers.
`AHandlerKeepsTheFunctionsIncomingValues` compiles and runs the emitted C++
at O0/O2 with real throws: a catch returns an incoming parameter or a value
computed before the try, or loads through the function's second parameter.
The latter must not become an uninitialized MSVC funclet-frame slot.
`ItaniumHandlerBodies.ACleanupOnlyPadBecomesACatchAllThatRethrows` prints a
pad that only cleans up as `try { … } catch (...) { cleanup; throw; }` and
keeps it labelled in C. `ACleanupScopeHoldsNoCallItsPadDoesNotCover` keeps a
call that reaches no pad out of the scopes, and
`ACopiedCallKeepsTheCoverOfItsInstruction` does so for a tail copy whose
statement took a covered jump's address.
`ABranchWhoseArmsCallThroughThePadIsOneScope` wraps the whole branch, and
`ACopyWithoutAnAddressKeepsItsCallsInstruction` places calls copied into both
arms by their instruction. `AnExceptionSpilledThroughAFrameAddressIsResumed`
follows the exception through the slot address clang keeps for a large frame.
`AnExceptionSpilledOffACopiedFrameBaseIsResumed` follows it through a copy of
the base clang reaches the far slots from,
`ASpillAndAReloadThroughTwoBaseCopiesMatch` through one copy to the spill and
another to the reload, and
`AReadThroughABaseRewrittenAfterTheSpillKeepsThePad` keeps the pad when the
base's slot changes between the spill and the copy.
`ACallOfNoInstructionKeepsTheCleanupPad`,
`AJumpIntoACleanupScopeKeepsThePad` and
`ACoveredCallOnlyAJumpReachesKeepsThePad` keep the pad where a scope cannot
be proved. `NothingFallsOutOfAnEndlessLoop` prints no dead statement after a
`while (1)` that only returns. `HighControlFlowSemantics.AMergedCallKeepsAnInstructionOnlyIfItHadOne`
checks that merging two branches' equal calls forgets their instructions.
Malformed unwind/prologue and converted-SP checks run with source projection
enabled too. `WindowsEHModesCorpus.DecompileMatrixFailsClosedWithAuditableExceptionMetadata`
runs the original eleven-case matrix, including the complete x64 xcpt4 image.
`DecompilesRegistrationCalleeProofCycles` gives its full PE32 applications a
240-second child-process allowance, within the corpus's 300-second CTest
deadline. This accommodates slower hosts producing the large source body;
the static proof work limits and output assertions do not change.

`RegisterPairReturnTest` checks x86 and ARM32 high-word evidence across
independent returns, transparent predecessors, clobbering calls, PHI inputs and
tail calls. `RegisterPairReturnPipeline` keeps a partial-register callee and a
`memset` veneer scalar despite callers reading EDX. The shared
`MedSSAMultiRoot.UnwrittenPhiEdgeCannotBorrowASiblingDefinition` checks x86,
x64, ARM32 and AArch64 merges. The PE32 xcpt4 corpus gate also requires the
three affected EH entries and the memset veneer to retain their bodies without
an unknown-return skeleton. These are source/IR checks, not native EH execution
certificates.

Run the original x64 executable locally and verify the separate source result:

```bash
python scripts/check_windows_xcpt4_source.py --neverd build-release/bin/neverd \
  --output /tmp/neverd-xcpt4-source --wine-prefix /tmp/neverd-xcpt4-wine64
```

The script accepts `wine`, `wine64` or `wine64-stable` (or `--wine`), uses an
isolated 64-bit prefix and checks all 90 reported cases even when the EXE exits
zero. An unhandled exception or page fault on either output stream rejects the
observation, including when Wine's debugger returns zero after all cases print
success. Routine Wine prefix diagnostics are allowed. The x64 fixture reports
89 successes and one explicit skip: test 29's
alignment check is compiled only for ARM. Unexpected skips fail. It then runs
the original source CLI and checks main's body, language/GS
metadata, that its local unwinds are jumps with filled `__finally` clauses, and
that it needs no unresolved-frame annotation. JSON keeps original runtime
and source-analysis results separate. Neither successful original execution
nor readable source is evidence that a replacement PE can execute. The Windows
EH CI lane runs this check and the full analysis matrix; source/patch refusal
and saved-slot overwrite controls remain required independently.

The pinned VS2019 PE32 GS/O2 xcpt4 fixture has five compile-time skips: test 29
requires ARM alignment handling, tests 58/61 require x64 nested-finally support,
and tests 87/89 exclude i386. Its original-runtime baseline therefore requires
85 successes, those five skips and no unhandled exception. Wine 9's built-in
UCRT can report a floating-point overflow while restoring `_controlfp_s` state
even though all 90 case reports appear and the launcher returns zero. For a
local comparison, use a dedicated `WINEARCH=win32` prefix with the Windows SDK's
x86 redistributable `ucrtbase.dll` in that prefix's `drive_c/windows/system32`,
and `WINEDLLOVERRIDES='ucrtbase=n'`. A `WINEDEBUG=-all,+loaddll` observation must
show that UCRT loaded as native. Preserve the original image hash, SDK version,
DLL hash, all case results and both output streams. This setup passes the
original PE32 fixture with Wine 9; it does not establish reconstructed-image
equivalence or replace native Windows replay.

`X64CRTFrame` in that target and `NeverDLiftTests` checks `_controlfp_s` output
extents with adjacent, partial-overlap, home-area, released-storage and return-PC
controls. Wrong providers, delay imports, missing or conflicting import storage,
unknown masks, unsupported precision control and previously escaped frames
refuse. Decoded WAIT and both register/memory scalar SSE arithmetic retain saved
frame identities, while malformed effects and GPR outputs (including R8 and
APX R16) do not. The shared PE32 floating-state tests cover the same policy.
Adding unproved language callbacks withdraws the Win64 FP preservation result.
These contracts leave the PE64 xcpt4 writable-format and runtime-activation
proofs open. Their native reconstruction coverage is separate from #858's
source-analysis acceptance above.

`RegistrationState.OrdinaryFinallyReturnsItsCheckedFrameEffects` checks actual
ordinary finally returns, private push/pop storage, incoming register values,
nonvolatile register changes and joins across both return arms. Missing branch
arms, return-PC corruption, administration writes, unknown aliases, opaque
calls, malformed boundaries, missing near-return evidence and stack-pop returns
reject. The check supplies no native callable contract and does not model the
nonlocal xcpt4 finally exits.

`RegistrationSEHReturn` checks the native near-return consumer against changed
CALL, callback, return occurrence and continuation identities, duplicate exits,
and multiple callers sharing one return. `RegistrationSEHControl` checks that
EH3 and EH4 both partition the physical CALL continuation before later source
instructions. The `normal-finally`, `eh4-normal-finally` and
`eh4-gs-normal-finally` reconstruction cases execute the generated callback,
public section/inplace installation and rebased images. Their independent
source replay also rejects replacing the generated finally return with
`unreachable`.

The nine `finally-parent-*` reconstruction cases and their EH4/EH4+GS variants
cover ordinary and runtime SavedESP branches, multiple parent destinations,
mixed near-return/nonlocal exits and another exception after resumption.
The parent-only ordinary and unwind cases resume code with no ordinary incoming
edge before joining an established parent epilogue. Their original and rebased
executions must pass independently. `FinallyOnlyParentTailsRequireEveryPathToAnAnchor`
checks single-block, chained and conditional tails in both block orders, with
cycles, missing/duplicate edges, foreign callbacks, decoded-target mismatches,
mode changes, guards and unanchored returns rejected.
They also check the current EBX/ESI/EDI values written by the finally and restore
the original caller's nonvolatile registers before returning. The register-input
case computes from the ordinary caller's values while retaining a scope that
is never activated by source try levels. Reentry checks run before the second
exception, whose handler has a separate runtime register contract.
Each case requires the original, independently installed outputs, both CLI
patch modes, IR/EXE inputs, optimization on/off and rebased images (20 runtime
observations). The reentry sources explicitly reconnect their live registration;
the unwind case additionally builds a control without this repair and requires
`RegistrationSEHParentExit.InputPE32RejectsAnAbandonedUnwindGuard` to reject it.
The invalid control is never counted or executed as a passing runtime fixture.
`RegistrationSEHParentExit` checks 37 changed source/invocation facts and complete
module rollback after failed outlining. `RegistrationSEHParentExitIRMutations`
checks 36 verifier-clean changes to capture, private storage, aliases, FS:[0],
selectors, source destinations and retained callback ABI. Callback-to-parent
PHI copies require the exact authenticated edge, including recovered scalar
slots shared by multiple destinations. The complete source replay profile
includes all 243 reconstruction cases and requires 4,860 runtime observations.
`RegistrationSEHRuntimeFrame.ParentResumeUsesTheBoundCallbackSpill` checks a
parent pointer spill written by its callback and read after a bound parent
resumption. Missing jump or edge bindings, full and partial pointer overwrites,
callback-local storage and a substituted entry capture must refuse. The EH3
and EH4 `finally-parent-reenter-unwind` cases cover the same address proof in
generated native code, with the abandoned-unwind-guard control still rejected.
`RegistrationSEHRegisterIRMutations` checks 30 edits to register slots, aliases,
source order, runtime-entry selection and constant outputs.
`RegistrationCookieABI` checks ECX-only recovery despite incidental EDX/XMM/stack
values and conflicting inferred signatures, cross-block cookie PHIs, and 18
invalid source occurrences that must not acquire the cookie-call protocol.
`RegistrationConditionalFrame.XCPT4SelectedFunctionRetainsItsScalarFilterRange`
checks that focused loading preserves the LowIR protected range and MedIR finally
returns even when the native parent-chain gate fails. The parent-exit tests require
both native preparation and independent COFF binding to reject that unsafe chain.

`RAMReservationTests.cpp` checks public write witnesses across identical-value and ABA stores, retained slices, address reuse, sibling mappings, rollback, cancellation, fault-prefix commits and opaque execution. `UnpackDriver.RelocationFactsRequireUninterruptedLoaderWrites` checks owned loader facts at preferred, downward and kernel load addresses: restored bytes do not restore invalidated provenance. `DriverGuardExecution.SessionFixupsInvalidateOriginalLoaderFacts` distinguishes active CFG pointer replacement from dormant fallback retention.

`UnpackDriver.SnapshotPreservesOnlyUnmodifiedLoaderRelocationFacts` checks PE output, an independent DIR64 reader, model rebasing and exclusion of rewritten debug records. `UnpackDriver.SnapshotRelocationFactsBindSourceAndFormatWrites` rejects source/base/order mismatches and excludes formatting replacements even when bytes match. These checks certify diagnostic metadata, not native recovery.

`RegistrationStackCopy.*` authenticates equal-displacement copies from both callback predecessors and rejects changed displacements, unknown or undefined sources, missing paths, external definitions, reads before definition, volatile stores and uninitialized self-copies.

## Source and native object replacement tests

The current expansion inventory is checked in as `unittests/Inputs/source-patch-expansion.json`: 283 CPU matrix cases, 14 layout cases, 16 callback cases, 265 exception-contract cases and the exact host-specific C API list. `scripts/qualify_source_patch_expansion.py` requires the complete inventory with zero failures or skips at a clean, exact source commit. `scripts/check_source_patch_expansion_runtime.py` separately executes callback, dependency and combined IR/object images through the native OS loader: 84 functional and 84 exception observations plus two missing-library/symbol controls per host. It checks real old/new shared libraries, floating/stack arguments, repeated saved-body calls, exactly-once cleanup, loader metadata and publication hashes. CPU, compatibility and native OS process evidence remain separate.

Six selected native OS/ISA jobs passed with zero failed or skipped cases: 3669 GoogleTest executions, 1008 native process observations (504 functional and 504 C++ exception observations), 12 real loader rejections, 96 images and 84 publication receipts.
