and rejects mixing physical transfers with local scalable SSA state. Predicate
instructions without a semantic contract are rejected through normal and fast
decoders in both strict and permissive modes. This is not native SVE execution
or privileged exception-return qualification.

`AArch64FunctionDiscovery` covers zero-based raw images, actual returning and
no-return calls, and distant branches into filler across scan chunks.
`MedVariadic.IntegerOnlyVaListMustNameItsOwnSpillChain` rejects a va_list whose
x7 copy is separate from its claimed contiguous argument save area.

Run `NeverDPipelineOutcomeTests`, `NeverDSessionCAPITests`,
`NeverDSessionLLVMTests`, `NeverDFunctionDisasmCAPITests`,
`NeverDSessionFunctionDiscoveryTests` and `NeverDWorkerConstantBranch` for
source-failure propagation, inferred extents, synthetic tail-call exclusion,
raw address disassembly and listing ownership. `FunctionDisasmSize` checks
adjacent and separated entries with unordered recovered blocks.
`NeverDWorkerConstantBranch` also recovers a callee before its caller and
checks that their shared tail keeps its declared, proven owner.
`CImageObjects.DeclaredObjectsHoldTheImageBytes` compiles and executes UTF-16
image declarations without requiring `uchar.h`, which macOS SDKs lack.

`LegacyBound/*` covers signed word/dword BOUND in both protected code widths,
legacy paging/PAE, all CPLs, segment choices, conditional upper-field access,
16/32-bit offset wrap and original #BR/#PF repair/IRET/retry. Repeat on each
qualified hybrid-core profile with `NEVERD_TEST_LEGACY_ALIGNMENT=before`.
`X86BoundSource.*` exports both C routes with
`NEVERD_ISA_REGRESSION_ARTIFACT_DIR`.

`X86ArplSource` in `NeverDX86VirtualizationSourceTests` checks both C writers,
native LLVM, old-SDK assembly fallback, ELF/COFF/MachO, live selector/ZF and
DS/FS/GS memory forms. It validates explicit native address widths and segment
prefixes and rejects weakened memory effects, speculative calls and wrong
modes. Stock Clang and the full LLVM fork own native legacy-code output;
NeverC has no ARPL source builtin. The separate `LegacyArpl` matrix owns
original-image execution and retry.

`X86HresetSource` checks native/fallback dispatch and function target attributes
on x86/x64 ELF/COFF/MachO, including ignored nonzero immediates. It also rejects
calls with weakened effects, the wrong calling convention or the wrong mode.
Preserve its exports with `NEVERD_ISA_REGRESSION_ARTIFACT_DIR`; NeverC's
`tests/neverc/X86/verify_hreset_source.py` recompiles each C file and checks the
exported ELF objects. It decodes HRESET before replacing it with a trap to
observe EAX and the resumed function return. Patched Clang/NeverC must use
native calls without a global `-mhreset`; stock Clang uses `--fallback`.
NeverC recompilation uses x64 targets only. This controlled observation does
not qualify physical history reset.

The LLVM/NeverC native far-transfer compiler checks live in the forks:
`llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/native-far-transfers.ll` covers O0/O2, code16/32/64,
x32, ELF/COFF/Mach-O, mode/type/immediate diagnostics and terminal adjacency.
NeverC's `X86FarTransferTest.*` checks C23 identities, returning/nonreturning
control, all six x64 memory builtins. The generated
instruction-table checker is `utils/lint/sync-x86-far-transfers.py`.

For native far-transfer execution, run NeverC's
`tests/neverc/X86/verify_far_transfers.py --llvm-bin LLVM_BIN --neverc NEVERC
--mode 64 --output OUTPUT` on a KVM-capable x86 host. It exercises direct LLVM,
NeverC and the IR bridge at O0/O2. Packed targets, terminal stack transport,
state/RAM, returned ABI values and deliberate corruption controls are checked.
Nonzero gate parameters, task switching, CET, faults and asynchronous unwinding
remain outside this compiler fixture.

The [2026-11-05 native far-transfer
qualification](evidence/x86-native-far-transfers-2026-11-05.json) records 32
O0/O2 profiles across P/E cores: 4,512 state pairs, 2,112 returning ABI checks
and 64 rejected corruption controls. All four LLVM lit tests, 25 NeverC
frontend regressions and 91 generated-table tests passed. NeverC's strict
global-state audit still reports the same 90 source-global findings as the
recorded baseline; this change adds none and does not weaken the audit.

`NeverDHighCallParameterForwardingTests` checks Win64 argument value identity. Full-width copies and agreeing PHIs may name an incoming parameter; masks, shifts and narrowing copies must retain their computed argument.

`HighControlFlowSemantics.UnusedValuesKeepPlainReadsAndTheirAddresses` checks that unused direct and nested ordinary loads retain their original address and evaluation in HighIR dead-value cleanup.

`HighControlFlowSemantics.SimplifierPublishesSharedReplacementAtEveryUse` checks shared DAG replacement publication in both root orders, independent return values and a stable second cleanup invocation.

Nested literal-tag comparisons retain original branch priority and unknown tails. `SymExpr` regressions exhaust small selectors, retain data-valued arms and check bounded inspection of a 4096-node tail.

`SymExpr.ConditionalConstantWindowsIgnorePredicatesAndRespectWork` and `ConditionalSlicesKeepDifferentAndUnknownArms` check branch-common constant windows, exact work refusal and differing or unknown arms.

`SymKnownBits` carrier, partial-cache and CONCAT refusal regressions check independent facts under exhausted child work and precision recovery on a later query without increasing query limits.

`SymKnownBits` bounded unsigned-remainder regressions cover dynamic nonzero divisors, possibly zero divisors, exhausted dividends and 8/16/32/64/128-bit bounds; the extracted-bit MBA regression checks that a consumer uses the fact without assuming division is partial.

`SymExpr.PlainVariableIndexKeepsLeafIdentityAcrossGrowthAndCopies` checks complete name/width identity, embedded NULs, growth, copies and repeated declarations without creating new nodes.

`SymExpr.LiteralSelections*` checks exact constant bitwise folding through selected literal carriers at 2--128 bits, with independent APInt evaluation and nonliteral-arm refusal controls. The builders retain narrow extension carriers and do not distribute data-valued arms.

`SymExpr` variable-membership checks compare structural membership with full variable collection, including context copies and missing IDs. Substitution checks retain unrelated shared payloads, exact root order, non-variable keys and simultaneous replacement semantics.

`SymState` memory-view regressions check whole-word overwrite node counts, independent byte-store equivalence, endian order, partial overwrites, modular relative coordinates and non-allocating materialized reads. Scalar snapshot and restore tests check that memory operations do not fork or replace unrelated scalar state.

`ActivityQueue.StrictPrioritySurvivesPrefixConsumptionAndReinsertion` uses an independent ordered-set oracle through queue copies, activity increases and reinsertion. The assumption-assigned queue regression checks every variable is restored after backtracking, with unchanged model and conflict behavior.

`X86CMov` regressions cover ordinary x86/x64 CMOV through the shared SELECT representation: all 16 conditions, all flag inputs, partial and zero-extending destination writes, unchanged source/flags, and unconditional memory reads that can fault before destination writes.

`NeverDMedPhiPlacementTests` checks a 128-value live join across x86, x64, ARM and AArch64: every required temporary has one complete PHI with its actual incoming edge identities. The membership index is independent of PHI output order.

`NeverDMedTempLivenessTests` checks that block-local temporary definitions need no join PHI, while cross-branch reads and loop-carried temporaries retain theirs. Register and stack carriers keep conservative implicit ABI-use handling.

`HighControlFlowSemantics.LargeSourceDropsUnobservedBitsButKeepsLoads` forces the large-function route and checks exact value cleanup without removing a still-observable memory read.

`HighSymSimplify.LargeConversionHonorsSymbolicOptInAndKeepsLoads` checks the symbolic option on the large-function route, with the option both on and off and with or without a real LOAD.

`HighControlFlowSemantics.LargeSourceNamesDeepConditionalValues` uses a reachable 1025-block function and deep conditional values. Independent HighIR execution checks both selected and unselected paths, and emitted C must contain no depth truncation or unknown-value placeholder.

MedStackAlignment reusable-entry query regressions exercise the existing scoped MedEntryStackOffsets owner after changed definitions, PHI relocation, new incoming edges and duplicate definitions. Repeated known/unknown queries cover four ISAs and three formats. These qualify the upstream implementation from 5b5e901d2 instead of adding a second proof cache.

`CDisplayFrameRecord` index regressions check duplicate-name owner precedence, layout replacement, current propagated types and disabled storage projection. The index is rebuilt with its layout snapshot; mutable types are read from their current slots.

The same suite rejects zero alignment masks, overflowing signed offset chains,
and overflowing alias/parent-frame rebases. It retains valid boundary
differences, target entry-stack residues, the existing traversal bound and
display-only roots without granting storage access. x86, x64, ARM, AArch64 and
both byte orders of MIPS32/64 exercise root checks. Typed pointer offsets,
frame overlays, member distances and alignment residues cover the adjacent
arithmetic boundaries. Both C writers execute a zero-masked frame address at
O0/O2 with undefined-behavior checks. Run `NeverDCDisplayFrameRecordTests` and
the complete C-pointer/source ABI suites after changing this walk.

`HighEntryStackOffsets.SharedIndexesKeepDefinitionAndPhiIdentities` checks register/temporary identities, ambiguous PHIs and a new conversion after mutation. Win64 forwarding checks use the same converter-owned definition and PHI indexes as production calls.

`HighControlFlowSemantics.RepeatedSplicesKeepMovedNestedEntriesCurrent` executes 32 selected cases through repeated nested block/if/switch moves and checks exact return values, retained stores and pinned entries. The sparse position index is local to one batch and preserves the existing incremental site/parent updates. It retains all address groups, retires edited or destroyed buffers, and updates source placeholders only over their changed range and following group. SpliceRebuildsKeepNewFallthroughEntriesAndUnchangedLists independently executes new fallthrough targets beside an unchanged scalar list through repeated rebuilds.

HighControlFlowSemantics external-skip tests independently execute all 256 branch choices and preserve earlier nested incoming edges. Batched external-skip ownership must retain statement order and reject outside entries; the current upstream goto-splice and entry-label indexes are retained. Windows exception regressions qualify exceptional control flow.

`HighExprSimplify.NamingCapturedReadsCleansTheirDeadValueConsumers` checks newly pure consumers after expression naming. Zero masks disappear while the captured load and its original address remain.

`NeverDHighFlagReadTests` covers unused/live EFLAGS images, malformed or unowned calls, branch anchors, exact owned x86/x64 LLVM assembly and retained write ordering. LLVM cleanup changes only the source clone; the original module and native code generation stay intact.

The scoped-search regressions compare retained and fresh HighIR semantic work while changing reaching definitions, operand aliasing, widths and thread limits, with independent integer evaluation. Only identical unsuccessful fixed-policy searches are retained; current definitions, effects and symbolic values are rebuilt at every call.

HighSymSimplify bitcast, low-prefix, Boolean/selection and incoming-PHI regressions compare exact APInt results and compiled C at O0/O2. Control splits, labels, ambiguous widths, calls, loads and assignment conversions retain their original scope and effect boundaries.

HighSymSimplify expanded-byte-parity tests preserve every input bit at 8/32/64-bit carrier widths and reject repeated-bit impostors. The generated source runs all 65536 signed-byte input pairs at O0 and O2. SymExec and the source bridge share the same population-count value definition; no additional x86 intrinsic capabilities are part of this fix.

HighExprSimplify exact-demand regressions independently check multiple readers, renamed local identities, loop arrivals, integer conversions, predicate scaling and compiled source. Deep discardability retains loads, calls, ordered accesses, malformed selections and possibly trapping division even when their result is unused. The current upstream wrapped-difference equality semantics are preserved.

HighExprSimplify selected-byte regressions recover only contiguous captured-local lanes with matching pure guards. Offset, sign-extension, different-guard, load and unknown-value controls remain unchanged; generated source executes at both result widths and optimization levels.

Common-word equality cancellation is covered by independent APInt evaluations at 1--256 bits. It cancels only identical complete XOR or additive operands; subtraction reuses the same additive collector. Packed word contents remain unconstrained.

SymExprCancellation captured-mask tests use independent exhaustive small-word and multiword APInt evaluation. Negative controls retain overlapping carries and uncovered fields; bounded known-bit queries leave unresolved inputs intact. Existing complemented-offset MBA tests qualify the equivalent normalized constructor forms.

`SymMBAFiniteSelection` checks exact small ordinal tables and shared Boolean selection trees through the ordinary `simplifyMBADeep` entry. APInt oracles and independent bitvector UNSAT checks cover 8--128 bits, wide out-of-range selectors, unknown defaults, duplicate priorities, complete shifted-bit trees and caller work/storage refusals. No sample-only candidate is published. Tables are read in one final pass that competes with the finished answer and uses only the work it left: a nested table keeps the value set its enclosing equality proves false, and a root whose measurement removes repeated tests keeps the shorter selection. One-condition selections and two-case ordinal chains keep their selection spelling.

SymConditionalControls and SymMBASelector Boolean-word tests use exhaustive small input tables and an independent solver check through 257 bits. Partial-mask and nonfitting-constant controls retain their data semantics; a large opaque predicate must not consume the budget before a complete root choice is recognized.

SymMBARewriteCache regressions compare cold/hot work counts rather than wall-clock thresholds. Completed unchanged subtrees, opaque parent compositions, refused siblings, working-set eviction and option/context/work boundaries retain exact derivation semantics. SymMBASparseContext additionally checks placeholder declaration reuse without hiding caller inputs or carrying declarations across contexts.

The refused-sibling case derives its allowance from one child's measured work
so faster analysis still reaches exhaustion between siblings. It checks both
the completed child's one-unit reuse and the unfinished sibling's remaining work.

`HighControlFlowSemantics.UnusedValuesDropReadsOfTheirOwnFrame` keeps unused reads through pointers and past the frame while dropping reads of the private frame, across stack-adjustment chains longer than one address walk. `HighCPointerAddresses.UnusedFieldLoadIsNotARegistersEntryValue` keeps a register's entry value from taking a later unused field load's name. `SymState.AnUnreadRunOfAPartlyKnownWordIsOneInput`, `SymMBARewriteCache.RecoveredWordChoicesStayInTheEvictionOrder` and `SymMBAKnownFacts.ConstantsBesideSeveralTermsStillFold` cover unread byte runs, cache eviction of recovered word choices and masks beside several terms. `HighControlFlowSemantics.UnusedOwnFrameReadsFollowEveryStackAdjustment` proves a read of the private frame through i386's sign-extended stack adjustment and in a function whose locals are all temporaries, so an unused reload no longer keeps its register's save. `HighCPointerAddresses.ImmutableSlotLoadsConvertTheirAddressOnce` converts a read-only GOT slot's address to an integer once. `HighControlFlowSemantics.StoreBetweenNestedTestsKeepsTheInnerTest` keeps an inner test of a slot that a store, or an assignment through it, changed after the outer test, as each block of the bounded graph in `BytecodeCLI.JoinedLoopBackEdgesKeepLabelsAndStateUpdates` does.

## MIPS ELF analysis and source roundtrips

The experimental [MIPS analysis](mips.md) path has focused targets
`NeverDMIPSTests` (ELF admission, endian data, GOT/PLT and unwind records),
`NeverDMIPSIntegerTests` (integer semantics and pinned Unicorn),
`NeverDMIPSFlowTests` (delay-slot ownership, capture and annulment),
`NeverDMIPSSDKTests` (physical disassembly rows and flow) and
`NeverDMIPSPipelineTests` (ABI recovery and both source paths).

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py build-mips --target NeverDMIPSTests NeverDMIPSIntegerTests NeverDMIPSFlowTests NeverDMIPSSDKTests NeverDMIPSPipelineTests neverd --parallel 4
ctest --test-dir build-mips --build-config Release -L '^NeverDMIPS.*Tests$' --output-on-failure --parallel 4
```

`unittests/lift/mips/roundtrip.py` is an additional standalone differential
runner. It needs clang and lld with MIPS targets, pyelftools, and the repository's
pinned Unicorn native library/Python bindings. Pass the built CLI, compiler,
linker and an ignored output directory explicitly:

```sh
LIBUNICORN_PATH=/path/to/repo-pinned-unicorn-library PYTHONPATH="$PWD/third_party/unicorn/bindings/python" python3 unittests/lift/mips/roundtrip.py --neverd build-mips/bin/neverd --clang /path/to/clang --ld /path/to/ld.lld --output build-mips/roundtrip
```

The runner compiles the owned assembly and each generated C variant for all
four width/byte-order profiles. It checks return values and memory effects,
including taken/untaken likely branches, delayed calls, argument carriers,
readonly/writable globals, image pointers, MUL, both word-merge orders,
doubleword merges and a merge read in an indirect call's slot. Uninitialized
merge destinations cover both orders, all offsets, fixed and seeded random
machine values, independent expected bytes and fault order at both page edges.
An invalid-memory branch-likely slot is tested both annulled and executed.
Bitfield and shuffle kernels cover all 13 classic SPECIAL3 forms and full-width
fields with independent bit/lane expectations. MIPS64 invalid word inputs are
tested separately as NeverD strict refusals, without executing architecturally
UNPREDICTABLE originals. These checks cover both an executed/annulled likely
slot and an instruction whose destination is `$zero`.
HighC merge globals are also executed with the original image unmapped.
LLVMC's original-image storage
and either route's omitted original callees are explicitly bound at their
original addresses; this qualifies the regenerated caller against that
dependency contract. It does
not claim a standalone rebuilt firmware. `results.json` records each case and
any failure, generated-source and binary hashes, and reclaimed bytes.
Per-function objects, executables and successful generated sources are retired
after each comparison. Once the workers have finished, the original profile
binaries are retired as well. Failures retain bounded diagnostics and verified
source evidence through the lifecycle contract below. An unavailable compiler
or oracle is a failure, not a skipped pass.
Vendor firmware remains outside the committed fixtures. Its separate static
receipt is [Archer C7 V5](firmware/archer-c7-v5.md).

Add `--encoding micro` to run the five microMIPS32/o32 leaves in both byte
orders and both C backends. This selects `micromips.S` and M14Kc, follows the
ELF symbol's callable tag, and preserves the original target on recompilation.
The ordinary four-profile run remains the default. Only the micro fixture's
functions may be selected with `--function` in that mode. The instruction-level
`MicroMIPSInteger` tests separately check independent literal memory encodings,
signed/unsigned loads, exact store bytes, failed writes and original-target
execution. Source numeric callable/import values remain explicitly unqualified;
the pipeline suite checks those refusals as well as ordinary leaf emission.

`MIPSDSPTests` in the integer target covers every control selector, ignored
selector bits, missing state, sticky flags, saturated byte and signed-halfword lanes,
rounded/non-rounded shifts, packing, expansion, replication, BITREV/RADDU,
destination/input aliases and discarded
results. Shift tests enumerate immediate and variable count boundaries against
independent expectations, including pure operations with absent DSPControl.
The pipeline target checks that DSPControl
effects survive both source routes without invented source arguments. Return
identity, standalone conversion, source shards and generated helper protection
have separate regressions.
`unittests/lift/mips/dsp-roundtrip.py` accepts the same explicit `--neverd`,
`--clang`, `--ld` and `--output` arguments as the ordinary runner. Its forty-two
owned `dsp.S` leaves check scalar results and DSPControl after returning, in
both byte orders and both C routes at `-O0` and `-O2`, with external `-mdsp`
enabled. It uses the pinned 74Kf model with
Status.MX enabled. A known original-model zero-destination overflow defect is
recorded separately; generated results must always satisfy the manual-derived
expectation. The managed artifact lifecycle retires each generated object and
executable after its comparisons.

The same runner exports standalone pure-shift and non-inlined wide-helper C
from `NeverDMIPSPipelineTests` beside the CLI, using
`NEVERD_MIPS_DSP_SOURCE_OUTPUT`. The sixteen additional source groups cover
both byte orders, both C routes and O0/O2 under external `-mdsp`. They observe
the complete o32 64-bit result, saved GPRs, stack, memory and post-return
DSPControl, and require actual helper entry. The standalone pure fixture has
no state-transfer intrinsic; negative target features must still prevent
compiler-introduced DSPControl writes.

`MIPSMSATests` covers scalar word transfers across all vector registers,
B/H/W/D carry and borrow boundaries, equality and signed/unsigned comparison
masks and signed/unsigned min/max lane selection, per-lane shifts, bit edits,
truncated multiplication/accumulation, absolute-magnitude min/max (ties select WT),
full-container logical operations and
aliasing, independent byte-wise expectations, missing state, decoder reuse and
P5600 reference execution. Loader cases check r5/MSA/CPR128/FP64 evidence;
pipeline cases check both source routes and unchanged refusals with/without an
Image. Shift counts cover zero, width-1, width, width+1 and high bits; the
independent oracle shifts individual bits and multiplies bytes. The owned MSA
source runner recompiles ninety-eight scalar/memory leaves
in both byte orders at O0/O2 through HighC and LLVMC. It checks each output byte
and the preserved F20/F22/.../F30 low64 values, maps original/generated ELF separately,
and retires scratch on success and failure:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=third_party/unicorn/bindings/python:scripts \
  LIBUNICORN_PATH=build-mips/roundtrip \
  python3 unittests/lift/mips/msa-roundtrip.py --neverd build-mips/bin/neverd \
  --clang /path/to/clang --ld /path/to/ld.lld --output build-mips/roundtrip-msa
```

The same runner exports LLVMC's live 128-bit funnel-shift fixture from
`NeverDMIPSPipelineTests` beside the CLI, recompiles it for both byte orders at
O0/O2, and compares execution with an arbitrary-precision integer oracle.
Storage-only 128-bit locals and address-taken external declarations receive
separate target syntax checks; those four checks do not claim linked execution.

### MIPS16 source qualification

`MIPS16Integer`, `MIPS16Memory`, `MIPS16Frame`, `MIPS16Flow`, `MIPS16Loader`,
`MIPS16SDK` and `MIPS16Pipeline`
cover unsigned/signed immediate boundaries, EXTEND/truncation, compact register
fields, immediate/variable shifts, comparisons, negation, both HI/LO multiply
halves, word quotient/remainder, short/extended frames, strict unsupported forms,
local ISA evidence, physical pagination,
two-byte slots, direct/indirect target modes and image-free return proofs.
Frame tests enumerate argument/static mappings, extended saved-register counts,
zero/max sizes, every partial-fault position, exact memory order, alignment and
32-bit wrap. Control tests cover return-target capture and call-link stores in
slots, frame-entry discovery, and leaf stack-return proofs through division.
Multiple register spills are distinguished from actual overlapping or unresolved
writes to the return slot. Source parameter tests retain the full o32/n64
carrier for low-byte/halfword reads, and DSP replication execution supplies
nonzero upper input bits so optimized source cannot assume caller extension.
DIV/DIVU cover MIN32/-1, all sign combinations, zero-result uncertainty, strict
word inputs on MIPS64, dead-result removal, and the explicit narrower nonzero
source domain. A guest zero check after DIV returns 42, while regenerated source
rejects that input; those executions are recorded separately as qualification
refusals, never equivalence successes. The classic runner also recompiles word quotient/remainder leaves
for both word sizes and byte orders.
Shared pipeline cases reject incoming or call-clobbered HI/LO in classic
MIPS32/64 and MIPS16 before either source route can erase an unknown return.
They distinguish fully defined joins and post-call overwrites, with and without
an image. Source multiply leaves observe HI and LO separately as well as together.
Image-free MIPS32 calls still require the separately documented target-mode
evidence; that refusal is checked separately from accumulator state. The shared
`NeverDNdOpEmulatorTests` checks that strict arithmetic and comparisons reject absent or partial
register/temporary operands before writing, including 128-bit operations.
The literal scalar/memory reference runs on pinned Unicorn's 24Kf model.
Memory tests cover all compact register fields, short/extended offsets,
PC alignment before displacement, transfer-head PC bases in slots, exact output
bytes, and LowIR fault order even for dead results. Call tests check physical
widths, tagged links, target capture, conflicting mode evidence in discovery
and rejection of unproved cross-call return identities.
`mips16-roundtrip.py` recompiles thirty-nine scalar/control/memory/call functions through HighC and
LLVMC, in both byte orders at O0/O2. It checks independent results, stack and
callee-saved GPR preservation, both incoming return-mode tags, ELF mode
flags and function tags under an adverse microMIPS compiler default.
An instruction in the caller's selected ISA executes after each return, so
checking only the canonical return address cannot hide a lost mode tag.
Call tests disable inlining and sibling-call optimization and require one actual
entry into the linked MIPS16 or classic callee. LLVMC callees are decompiled and
linked as separate objects, retaining their ELF mode tags. PC-pool accesses and
LLVMC original-storage declarations retain the original data mapping. GNU MIPS
as and ld are required; LLVM's integrated assembler/linker do not qualify this
MIPS16 route. Pass the executables explicitly:

```sh
LIBUNICORN_PATH=/path/to/repo-pinned-unicorn-library \
  PYTHONPATH=third_party/unicorn/bindings/python \
  python3 unittests/lift/mips/mips16-roundtrip.py --neverd build-mips/bin/neverd \
  --clang /path/to/clang --assembler /path/to/mips-as --ld /path/to/mips-ld \
  --output build-mips/roundtrip-mips16
```

The runner retires each generated source, assembly, object and ELF after its
readers finish; commands, hashes, observations and bounded failure evidence
remain. Source memory equivalence requires valid, accessible, target-aligned
ordinary RAM accesses; ordinary dead-load fault delivery remains unqualified
as documented in [MIPS support](mips.md#ordinary-memory-source-qualification).
These functions do not qualify omitted MIPS16 instructions or general ABI forms.

### MIPS16e2 and additional DSP/MSA arithmetic

`MIPS16E2` checks all 30 admitted encoding forms in both byte orders, compact
register aliases, bitfield limits, zero sources, GP memory widths, partial merge
footprints and reused-decoder feature evidence. `MIPS16E2Pipeline` checks exact
physical delay-slot widths and writable image-store bindings. Shared scalar
store tests exercise every alignment, narrow writable spans, absent inputs and
failure without partial writes. `MIPSCallMemory` checks that a partial overwrite
invalidates a spilled callee or stack argument while preserving already
captured registers. SELECT tests distinguish missing/unknown chosen
values from unobserved arms and retain all 128 result bits.

`mips16e2-roundtrip.py` recompiles the e2 fixture through both source backends
at O0/O2 with adverse microMIPS defaults. It uses the same explicit tool arguments
as `mips16-roundtrip.py`, with an output such as `build-mips/roundtrip-mips16e2`.
The input is assembled with GNU `-mmips16e2` and its ABI flag checked. Generated
old-MIPS16 code executes against manual-derived results, output memory, saved
registers and both caller ISA tags. The pinned Unicorn cannot execute original
e2 correctly; the report explicitly excludes that oracle and records no
original-e2 equivalence claim.

DSP word/carry tests cover sticky overflow, carry replacement versus
preservation, condition-bit replacement, byte/halfword PICK, zero destinations,
register aliases and missing state. MSA adds all four widths of absolute add,
saturating add/subtract and signed/unsigned average/rounded average. Independent
widened APInt expectations cover MIN+MIN, unsigned carries, negative ties and
aliased complete vectors. The DSP/MSA source runners compare originals and both
regenerated C routes under the pinned enabled 74Kf/P5600 models, including
DSPControl and saved low FPR views. The pinned reference fixes MSA signed-limit
construction and absolute `INT64_MIN` magnitudes, with QEMU's required wrapping
arithmetic enabled in CMake builds. All regenerated execution and the newly
added original-instruction fixtures must match independent results. The
reference also fixes discarded packed-DSP/shift results: helpers still update
DSPControl and enforce DSP enablement. The source runner permits no original
zero-destination mismatch; see the [DSP reference boundary](mips.md#classic-mips32-dsp-state-and-packed-arithmetic).
Reports identify the source revision and actual loaded native-library hash.
Ordinary pair padding, predecessor memory barriers,
single-sided barriers at joins, depth/work exhaustion and non-entry analysis
roots or exceptional/disconnected paths have separate call-recovery regressions.

MIPS16 delay-slot classification exhausts all 65,536 halfwords, both byte orders
and physical sizes. A shared jump normalizer avoids full scalar normalization
in slot queries. EHB/SYNC tests retain every stype, reject malformed shapes and
reserved fields, and prove SAVE/barrier/RESTORE source output in HighC and
LLVMC. The e2 runner compiles and executes each barrier's generated source and
checks its native assembly at O0/O2. This is not original-e2 or multiprocessor
ordering execution evidence.
Selected-function LLVMC regressions require the source-only helper definitions,
including when an input function collides with a barrier helper's name.
Deferred imports and named call hints are checked in both instruction/function
orders, including reserved suffixes and canonical import-storage-only evidence.
DSP ABS/SHLL tests cover signed extrema, every count, sticky fields, aliases,
zero destinations and missing state; CMPGU requires no DSPControl input.
MSA tests enumerate all 128 BIT fields and 256 byte immediates, unary count
extrema, all vector bytes, old-destination dependence and three-register aliases.
The source fixtures observe complete output memory and post-return state.

The [2026-11-10 evidence](evidence/mips16e2-dsp-msa-2026-11-10.json) separates
the final dev/ABI integration's correctness runs from the same-base feature
performance measurements. It includes the four failing-then-passing stack-lane
regressions, exact product/dependency hashes, six fresh source matrices, the
firmware output comparison and the location of local optimization controls.
Original e2 hardware execution and SMP/device ordering remain outside this
qualification.

### MIPS decode/lift and firmware performance

`neverd-mips-bench` is an opt-in target, excluded from the default build:

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py build-mips --target neverd-mips-bench --parallel 4
build-mips/bin/neverd-mips-bench mips64el lift /path/to/owned-code.bin 100000
```

Profiles are `mips`, `mipsel`, `mips64`, `mips64el`, `micromips`,
`micromipsel`, `mips16`, `mips16el`, `mips16e2`, `mips16e2el`, `mipsdsp`,
`mipsdspel`, `mipsmsa` and `mipsmsael`. The e2 profiles add explicit MIPS16e2
feature evidence to MIPS16 encoding. The DSP profiles explicitly select the admitted classic32 DSP
capability; MSA profiles select classic32 r5/o32 FP64 with the admitted integer
vector instructions.
Stages are `capstone`
(direct physical decoding), `decode` (NeverD physical decoding) and `lift`
(decoding plus LowIR, including delay slots). Both decode paths request the same
selected encoding/revision profile, detail on and text off. The pinned Capstone fork suppresses
rendered operand detail with text off; these physical decode measurements consume
instruction sizes and IDs. The harness reuses decoder handles, counts physical
instructions/LowOps and validates output fingerprints outside
the timed loop. Invalid, truncated or unsupported input fails. Direct Capstone
does not supply lift semantics and is not a decompiler throughput comparator.

`tools/neverd-bench/mips-paired.py` alternates baseline/candidate runs, warms each
job and retains CPU, wall, RSS, output hashes and every sample in an ignored
output directory. It accepts matching CLI/SDK/benchmark directories, raw files
named `PROFILE-unchanged.bin`, the retained Archer C7 `ubus`, dependency snapshots
from `neverd-dependency-inputs.json`, and JSON toolchain manifests with `compiler`,
`llvm`, `capstone` and `build` entries. Record exact versions/hashes, build flags
and allocator selection in those manifests before each build; unequal inputs
are refused. Run `--help` for explicit paths and repetition counts.
The default measures the four classic profiles. Repeat `--profile` to select
other profiles supported by both binaries, supplying the corresponding
`PROFILE-unchanged.bin` files; unsupported baseline instructions are errors.

Each baseline CLI must load its own matching SDK; the runner sets its library
search path accordingly. It checks output identity for the selected `call`
handler and discovered functions (limited to 250), with one/default threads and
both C backends. New instruction coverage and additional strict checks are
different work and require separate reporting, not same-output speedup claims.
This small corpus and a shared host do not establish a cross-tool ranking.

Both MIPS Python drivers reuse their `--output` directory through
`scripts/mips_validation_artifacts.py`. A new output must be empty; older,
unmarked reports are never adopted or deleted. Keep SDKs, firmware, fixture
inputs and pending comparison baselines outside that directory. The drivers
read those inputs in place and do not copy or install SDKs.

Generated objects, ELFs, successful C output and full per-command logs live in
owned scratch storage. Each completed roundtrip removes its temporary files;
the driver also removes scratch after failure or normal interruption. A later
start reclaims scratch left by an uncatchable kill. One output lock, inherited
by the compiler/CLI, prevents another invocation from reclaiming a surviving
reader's files. This lock is separate from the existing build lock because the
drivers never mutate the build cache or CTest's `LastTest.log`.
The recorded process group also protects descendants that close inherited file
descriptors. Scratch stays in place if a descendant outlives its command leader.
A kill during the spawn handoff, before the process group was recorded, requires
a reader audit; missing process identity is never treated as permission to
delete. These drivers use POSIX process groups and locks.

The reusable output retains the latest semantic/timing receipts and command
hashes, with up to 8 KiB of diagnostic tail for each failed command. Failed
generated sources are deduplicated by SHA-256 and verified after copying;
only the current and preceding run's source evidence remain. This retention
contract applies to newly owned validation output, not preexisting recovery
archives or user files. Copy a receipt needed for a separate comparison outside
the run directory before reusing it. Performance output disagreement retains
both differing sources and blocks a timing claim.

Run the small producer lifecycle checks without building a new SDK:

```sh
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/tests/test_mips_validation_artifacts.py -v
```

They exercise repeated success/failure, SIGTERM, SIGKILL recovery, surviving
child readers, preserved inputs and the actual paired-measurement entry point
with tiny fake commands. The roundtrip compiler-failure entry check uses the
local pinned Unicorn bindings when available. These are artifact lifecycle
checks, not performance or ISA qualification measurements.
